The restoration project is currently in the design phase with anticipated construction to begin in 2024. The County hired WSP, with Mote Marine Laboratory, to design the project.

Project_Description: Hurricane Ian’s landfall on Sanibel flattened the island's beach and dune areas. As the storm surge from Ian receded, significant erosion occurred resulting in the creation of channeled gullies along Sanibel's coastline. The Post Hurricane Ian Emergency Berm/Beach Recovery project placed approximately 389,401 tons of sand to restore the beach berm (dune) and fill gullies created by the receding storm surge. 15,859 truck loads (~389,401 tons) of sand were hauled to Sanibel Island for the project and it took 92 days of sand placement.
Habitat_Description: Sanibel Island beach and dune areas
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: An existing impoundment was repurposed as a filter marsh and BMPs that is estimated to remove about 430 lbs of nitrogen a year and about 100 lbs of Phosphorus a year. This project was led by Lee County Natural Resources Department with the help of a Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) grant.
Habitat_Description: Open Land, Mangrove Swamp/Wetland Hardwood Forest
Main_Funding_Source: Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP), Lee County
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Lee County Conservation 20/20 Land Acquisition - Estero Bay (Nom 630)
Project_Description: Lee County Conservation 20/20 program purchased a 7.69-acre property adjacent to Estero Bay Preserve State Park.
Habitat_Description: Mangrove Swamp, Wetland Hardwood Forest
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Nature Conservancy in Florida and the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) joined together to purchase a conservation easement at G Road Grove, an active citrus grove and tree nursery in key panther habitat.  G Road Grove joins a network of protected lands that expands the area within the Florida Panther Dispersal Zone, a 30,000-acre corridor in Hendry and Glades counties. This land helps connect the panthers' current breeding population in areas south of the Caloosahatchee River to suitable habitat north of the river. Florida panthers depend on these lands for safe movement and reliable food sources. Notably, the grove is home to prey species such as white-tailed deer and invasive feral hogs, which panthers help control.
Habitat_Description: Agriculture, Citrus Groves
Main_Funding_Source: U.S. Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service (USDA NRCS), The Nature Conservancy (TNC)
Lead_Implementer: U.S. Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service (USDA NRCS)
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Cape Coral Golf Club Land Acquisition
Project_Description: The City of Cape Coral purchased the property that is known as the former Cape Coral Golf Club for $10,400,000.
Habitat_Description: Golf Course, Open land, Residential
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Edward Chance Preserve - Coker Prairie Tract Invasive Plant Control
Project_Description: The Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD) completed maintenance control of any invasive plant species on the Edward Chance Preserve - Coker Prairie Tract property. Approximately 220 acres were covered and treated for species including: cogon grass, old world climbing fern, natal grass, and Brazilian pepper trees.
Habitat_Description: Mesic flatwoods, scrub, scrubby flatwoods
Main_Funding_Source: Southwest Florida Water Management District Vegetation Management Section
Lead_Implementer: Southwest Florida Water Management District Vegetation Management Section
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Sarasota County ESLPP E. Venice Avenue Property
Project_Description: Sarasota County's Environmentally Sensitive Lands Protection Program (ESLPP) purchased 5 acres of land at 3905 East Venice Ave, Venice, FL. The property was purchased on April 12, 2024. The property is part of a corridor along the River Road and the Wild and Scenic Myakka River. The property serves as a puzzle piece connecting already protected greenspace to the north at Sleeping Turtles South and property to the south at Jelks Preserve. The acquisition will expand and protect the wildlife corridor while also providing environmental education and nature-based recreational opportunities.
Habitat_Description: Remnant scrubby flatwoods. Variety of vegetation including saw palmetto, slash pine, several oak species, gallberry, fetterbush, broomsedge bluestem, and little bluestem.
Lead_Implementer: Brie Ondercin, Land Acquisition Coordinator for Parks, Recreation and Natural Resources of Sarasota County
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Sarasota County ESLPP Burns Property Acquisition
Project_Description: Sarasota County's Environmentally Sensitive Lands Protection Program (ESLPP) purchased a 43.34-acre parcel in North Port for $1.45 million on April 4, 2024. The Burns property consists of pasture, marshes and mixed hardwood hammock habitat. Wildlife sightings on the property include eastern wild turkey, crested caracara, swallow-tailed kite and sandhill cranes. The property was targeted as a Deer Prairie Creek Preserve protection priority site.
Habitat_Description: Upland forest, cropland, wet prairie
Lead_Implementer: Sarasota County Parks, Recreation and Natural Resources Department
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Myakka Ranchlands Florida Forever Project 4L's Ranch Acquisition
Project_Description: FDEP purchased a 1,531-acre easement located within the Florida Wildlife Corridor. Between Myakka Watershed and the Peace River Watershed, the land provides important protection to water quality and quantity. The property provides habitat for species including the crested caracara, Florida sandhill crane, Florida burrowing owl and Southeastern American Kestrel and gopher tortoise. The Myakka Ranchlands project is comprised of multiple tracts to the north and south of Myakka River State Park. The goals of the project are to expand and buffer diverse habitats, conserve land containing rare plant and animal species, and to protect, restore and maintain the quality and natural functions of land, water and wetland systems.
Habitat_Description: Upland areas such as mesic flatwoods, wetland depression marshes, wet prairie, and improved pasture
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The City of Cape Coral completed a shoreline mangrove planting at Coral Pointe Canal. This project will improve the long-term health and resilience of the ecosystem through mangrove restoration efforts. Mangroves provide numerous ecological, economic, and social benefits such as erosion control, biodiversity, water quality, climate change mitigation, recreation and aesthetics, fisheries support, and hurricane and storm surge protection. For this effort, the City planted 160 Red Mangroves and hydro-seeded the bank with grasses and wildflowers, as well as targetted sections where the shoreline mangroves are sparse to ensure bank stabilization.
Habitat_Description: Canal, shoreline, mangrove
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The City of Cape Coral partnered with Cape Christian to plant cocoplum and firebush at Rotary Park. The planting project was completed in April 2024.
Habitat_Description: Dry Prairie, Urban, Open land
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Deer Prairie Creek Invasive Plant Control
Project_Description: The Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD) completed maintenance control of invasive plant species at Deer Prairie Creek. Approximately 1519 acres were covered and invasives treated within those areas for species including cogon grass, old world climbing fern, Brazilian pepper trees, and melaluca trees.
Habitat_Description: Mesic flatwoods, scrub, scrubby flatwoods
Main_Funding_Source: Southwest Florida Water Management District Vegetation Management Section
Lead_Implementer: Southwest Florida Water Management District Vegetation Management Section
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Addition
Project_Description: This project is a new acquisition for preservation and restoration of cypress and other wetlands adjacent to the existing preserve.
Habitat_Description: This is a new addition adjacent to the exisiting Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of cypress slough and forested wetlands. There are some exotic invasive vegetation (primarily Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper) and animals (wild hogs).
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral Restoration
Project_Description: Recent restoration activities in the Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral parcel focused on exotic invasive vegetation removal, primarily Australian pines and Brazilian pepper, and endangerd species monitoring, supported by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Integrated Pest Mangement funds and Florida Parks Service in-kind staff match.
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral parcel habitats in cude mesic pine flatwoods, mangrove wetlands, riparian tidal creeks.
Main_Funding_Source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Recent restoration activities at Prairie Creek Preserve focused on exotic invasive vegetation removal, primarily of cogon grass.
Habitat_Description: Prairie Creek Preserve is a Conservation Charlotte acquistion located in Port Charlotte. The vast majority of the property is comprised of a mixture of upland habitats that have been well maintained by prescribed fires. The  habitats include scrub, scrubby flatwoods, palmetto prairies and pine flatwoods. There are also small areas of herbaceous marshes and improved pasture on the property. Prairie Creek traverses through the center of the property. The property provides habitat for several listed species of wildlife, including the Florida scrub-jay, gopher tortoises and eastern indigo snake.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This parcel was acquired in December 2008 for preservation and retoration and adjoins to existing Conservation 2020 parcels making up the Pine Island Flatwoods Preserve. The parcel is co-managed with volunteers from the Calusa Land Trust.
Habitat_Description: This newly acquired parcel connects 2 exisiting preservation parcels and includes the primary native plant comminities associated with mesic pine flatwoods and hydric hammock.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Don Pedro Restoration
Project_Description: Recent restoration activities at the Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Don Pedro parcel focused on hydrologic restoration, including removing fill and installing culverts and exotic invasive vegetation removal (10 acres). Also, public outreach included installing new signs regarding the value of wetlands and estuaries, as well as public wading programs. Funding was provided by the Gulf of Mexico Foundation ($56,000), the Barrier Island Parks Society ($5,000) with Florida Park Service ($56,000) and Charlotte Harbor Environmental Center ($500) in-kind staff match, plus many volunteer hours ($2,500).
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Don Pedro parcel habitats include native and disturbed tidal mangrove swamps and saltmarsh wetlands.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Restoration projects at Deep Lagoon include removal of exotic invasive vegetation (Brazilian pepper, Australian pines and melaleuca) and hydrologic restoration of agricultural, mosquito and flood ditches on disturbed tidal swamp and marshes, wet prairies, prairie hammocks, mesic flatwoods and abandoned flower nursery agricultural fields.
Habitat_Description: Deep Lagoon Preserve is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located along the south shore of the Caloosahatchee River. Natural plant communities include tidal swamps, tidal marshes, coastal grasslands, wet prairies, prairie hammocks and mesic flatwoods. The preserve provides habitat for several listed animal and plant species, including bald eagle,  nest  and smalltooth sawfish.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Buck Creek Preserve was acquired through Conservaton Charlotte in August 2006 for preservation, rstoration and enhanced public acess to natural resources. In October 2008,  Florida Communities Trust reimbursement Conservation Charlotte $3,400,000 towards the acquisition price of $8,400,000.
Habitat_Description: Buck Creek Preserve is a Conservation Charlotte Preserve located in Cape Haze, Florida. The entire 80+ acre parcel is comprised of native habitats. The majority of the site is scrubby flatwoods and mesic pine flatwoods. These flatwoods transition into coastal hammock and mangrove swamp along the creek. Buck Creek flows into Lemon Bay, an aquatic preserve and Outstanding Florida Water. The uplands on the site exhibit signs of fire suppression and many areas are succeeding into mesic oak and xeric hammocks. Mechanical restoration strategies will enable the property to be restored to its historical significance. These overgrown flatwoods are interspersed with open areas where gopher tortoise burrows are present. There is also an active bald eagle’s nest on the site. Listed wading birds frequently forage along the banks of Buck Creek. It is one of the largest areas of unprotected native habitat remaining on the Cape Haze Peninsula.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Myakka River State Park Habitat Restoration
Project_Description: Recent restoration activities in Myakka River State Park focused on exotic invasive animal removal (650 wild hogs)and exotic invasive plant removal, which included roller chopping (155 acres), tree-cut mowing (84 acres), prescribed burning (4,144 acres)and removal or treatment of cogon grass (73 acres), air potato (25 acres), Guinea Grass (9 acres), West Indian marsh grass (2.5 acres)and Old World climing fern, rosary pea, Brazilian, Casear's weed, Melaleuca, tropical soda apple, and wild taro (less than 1 acre each).
Habitat_Description: Myakka River State Park has a variety of native upland and wetland habitats: forested wetlands, including mesic pine flatwoods, hardwood and oak hammocks, cypress domes freshwater marshs and dry prairies. The dry priaries include many species of grasses, sedges, herbs and shrubs with sal malmetto, fetterbush, staggerbush, tar flower, gall berry, blueberry, wiregrass, carpet grasses and various bluestems. There are also exotic invasive animals, primarily wild hods,and exotic invasive plants, including air potato cogon grass, common banboo, guinea grass (Panicum maximum), rosary pea, West Indian marsh grass, Brazilian pepper, Cesear's wee, seaside mahoe, tropical soda apple, Melaleuca and wild taro.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Removal of exotic, invasive vegetation and animals and other wetland restoration activities in the 1290 acre Caloosahatchee Creeks Preserve along the northern shoreline of the Caloosahatchee River and managed by Lee County Conservation 2020.
Habitat_Description: Riverine shoreline, tidal influence, freshwater wetlands
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Recent habitat restoration activities focused on exotic invasive vegetation removal, including Melaleuca, cogon grass, Cesar weed, Australian pine, earleaf acacia and Brazilian pepper.
Habitat_Description: Pop Ash Creek Preserve is a 307 acre Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in northeast Lee County that was acquired in 2003. The preserve consists of both human-altered and natural plant communities that are mostly wet or mesic flatwoods and a portion of a blackwater stream -Popash Creek. Along the northern portion of Popash Creek, which was previously dredged, a lone pop ash tree (Fraxinus caroliniana) survives adjacent to larger Carolina willow (Salix caroliniana) and Brazilian pepper (Schinus terebinthifolius) trees. Past land uses and hydrologic modifications have disturbed about 90% of the Preserve.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Habitat restoration activities during this past year focused on exotic vegetation removal of Melaleuca on the 31 acres acquired in 2008.
Habitat_Description: Charlotte Harbor Buffer Preserve (CHBP) contains nine parcels totally about 400 acres adjacent to the Charlotte Harbor Preserves State Park. The Preserve contains several plant communities including pine flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods, scrub, oak hammock, tidal salt flats, tidal marsh, tidal swamps, and a disturbed Australian pine monoculture.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Prairie Creek Preserve was acquired by Conservation Charlotte in August 2008 for preservation, restoration and inhanced public acess to natural resources.
Habitat_Description: Prairie Creek Preserve is a Conservation Charlotte acquistion located in Port Charlotte. The vast majority of the property is comprised of a mixture of upland habitats that have been well maintained by prescribed fires. The habitats include scrub, scrubby flatwoods, palmetto prairies and pine flatwoods. There are also small areas of herbaceous marshes and improved pasture on the property. Prairie Creek traverses through the center of the property. The property provides habitat for several listed species of wildlife, including the Florida scrub-jay, gopher tortoises and eastern indigo snake.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Restoration 2010
Project_Description: The Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Restoration 2010 project focused on removal of exotic invasive animals (over 50 hogs were trapped), as well as removal of exotic invasive vegetation (including Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca).
Habitat_Description: The Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Additions for 2010 project is located in Lee County and is a Conservation 2020 preserve of about 2,267 acres, comprised of cypress slough and forested wetlands. There is some exotic invasive vegetation (primarily Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper) and animals (primarily wild hogs).
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Prairie Pines Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive exotic  animals (over 50 wild hogs were trapped) and vegetation, primarily Brazilian pepper Melaleuca.
Habitat_Description: The Prairie Pines Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve includes 2,654 acres and consists of a mosaic of several native plant communities, including wet and mesic flatwoods, depression marshes, wet prairies, prairie hammocks and a small baygall. Past agricultural practices have disturbed about 7% of the Preserve.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Shoreline Stabilization and Habitat Enhancement in the Mullock Creek Basin
Project_Description: The Shoreline Stabilization and Habitat enhancement in the Mullock Creek Basin project focused on removing 180 linear fee of invasive exotic vegetation, including Melaleuca, Brazilian pepper and air potatoes, removal of garbage, removal of sediments that were placed along the shoreline and planting of native vegetation. Private landowners, volunteers and university students participated in the project.
Habitat_Description: The Shoreline Stabilization and Habitat Enhancement in the Mullock Creek Basin project is in San Carlos Park in Lee County on residential lots adjacent to the East Mullock Drainage District Canal. The altered shoreline is steep, high and covered with invasive non-native shrubs, grasses and trees.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Orange River Preserve Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive exotic  vegetation, primarily Melaleuca, but including Caesar Weed, and Brazilian pepper, with prescribed fire being planned. Volunteer workdays include assistance from Cape Coral Environmental Club and Florida Gulf Coast University students.
Habitat_Description: The Orange River Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve is over 58 acres in size and consists of three plant communities: scrubby flatwoods, mesic hammock and tidal swamp.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Alligator Creek Restoration 2010
Project_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Alligator Creek Restoration 2010 project focused on removal and treatment of invasive exotic vegetation, primarily Australian pines and Brazilian pepper.
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Alligator Creek Restoration 2010 project is located in Charlotte County and is managed by the Florida Parks Service. The primary habitats include native and disturbed mesic pine and scrubby flatwoods, freshwater wetlands, tidal mangrove swamps, salt marsh and salt terns with exotic invasive plants including Brazilian pepper, Australian Pine, Melaleuca, old world climbing firm and air potato.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Daniels Preserve at Spanish Creek Restoration 2010
Project_Description: The Daniels Preserve at Spanish Creek Restoration 2010 project focused on invasive exotic plant control, primarily Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca, gopher tortoise habitat enhancement and invasive exotic animal control (over 25 wild hogs were trapped).
Habitat_Description: The Daniels Preserve at Spanish Creek Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve includes 243 acres of 21 plant communities and includes the headwaters of Spanish Creek. The dominant plant communities are pine flatwoods, oak hammocks, improved pasture, wetlands forested mixed, and pine-mesic oak.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Walton Ranch Land Acquisition focuses on purchasing the agricultural parcel to preserve and restore native forested upland and wetland habitats.
Habitat_Description: The Walton Ranch Land Acquisition project is located in eastern Sarasota County between the Myakka and Peace Rivers. The parcel includes 3,795 acres of forested uplands, wetlands, range, pasture, row crop and sod agriculture.
Main_Funding_Source: South West Florida Water Management District
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Tippecanoe Environmental Park Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010
Project_Description: The Tippecanoe Environmental Park Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project focused on treating primarily Brazilian pepper and Australian pine with girdling and herbicide  applications. Approximately 10 acres was treated this FY. No native vegetation has been replanted where the Brazilian pepper has been removed because the native vegetation recruits successfully on it's own.
Habitat_Description: The Tippecanoe Environmental Park Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. Tippecanoe Environmental Park is a 380 acre preserve consisting of oak scrub, scrubby flatwoods, pine flatwoods, coastal hammock, floodplain forest, salt marshes and mangrove swamps. Tippecanoe is home to a family of Florida Scrub Jays, as well as a large population of gopher tortoises. Boardwalks provide visitors the opportunity to observe the bird life within the mangroves and look out over the marshes.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Smokehouse Bay Preserve Restoration project focused on restoring natural hydrology and vegetation and treating non-indigenous invasive vegetation. The abandoned palm grove ditches and furrows were re-grading ditches to a more natural slope, invasive vegetation was treated and native vegetation was planted.
Habitat_Description: Smokehouse Bay Preserve Restoration project is located on northern Pine Island in Lee County, adjacent to Matlacha Pass. The 268 acre parcel is a Lee Co Conservation 2020 preserve and the habitats include abandoned palm groves which were previously ditched and slope into mangrove swamp and the Smokehouse Bay estuary. Much of the preserve consists of relatively intact native wetland vegetation.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Maxine Barritt (Tramonto Vista) Park and Nature Preserve Restoration
Project_Description: The Maxine Barritt Park and Nature Preserve project activities focus on restoring native vegetation, including live oaks, cabbage palms, dune sunflowers and sea grapes, establishing a dune crossover to the beach and a sunset-viewing platform, and installing public use amenities designed for passive use and nature observation.
Habitat_Description: The Maxine Barritt (Tramonto Vista) Park and Nature Preserve is located in Venice in Sarasota County. The nature preserve is located on disturbed grass sod habitat with non-native trees on a land parcel that was formerly a former sewage treatment plant and pond.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Canal and Seawall Mangrove Vegetation Plantings
Project_Description: The Canal and Seawall Mangrove Vegetation Plantings project focused on developing planting guidelines, preparing and planting mangrove seedlings (mixed species) at proper elevations along residential parcels with seawalls along canals and tidal creeks, as well as educating residents on the importance of mangrove ecosystems.
Habitat_Description: The Canal and Seawall Mangrove Vegetation Plantings project is located in Lee County on 20 privately owned residential lots adjacent to canals and tidal creeks. The habitat on the residential parcels is primarily disturbed grass sod with some remaining native upland and wetland trees.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Oak Creek Preserve project focused on acquisition of lands for preservation and restoration of native forested uplands and forested wetlands adjacent to Oak Creek.
Habitat_Description: The Oak Creek Preserve is a Lee County Conservation 2020 acquisition located in Lee County in Bonita Springs. The primary habitats are forested uplands and forested wetlands, including oak palm hammock, slash pines, cypress, live oak, sable palm, laurel oak, native ferns, bromeliads resurrection ferns, coral vine and Spanish moss. The parcel is located on both sides of Oak Creek, a tributary to the Imperial River.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Community Based Oyster Restoration in Clam Bayou
Project_Description: The Community Based Oyster Restoration in Clam Bayou project focused on deployment of oyster shell substrate to enhance natural oyster recruitment, settling and growth at sites located in a tidally flushed lagoonal estuary were hydrologic restoration was recently completed. The project involved many partners and citizen volunteers and provided significant public education and community involvement.
Habitat_Description: The Community Based Oyster Restoration in Clam Bayou project is located in Lee County in a tidally inundated lagoon where hydrologic restoration was recently completed. The primary habitats are seagrass, unvegetated mudflats, mangroves and oysters. The oyster restoration sites provide settling areas for juvenile oyster spat. The oyster restoration project is a partnership between Sanibel Captiva Conservation Foundation, NOAA and community volunteers.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Charlotte Flatwoods Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010
Project_Description: The Charlotte Flatwoods Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project focused on removing slash pines from fire dependant natural communities to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species. The timber thinning was done by Conservation Charlotte staff.
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Flatwoods Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. Charlotte Flatwoods is 487 acres of mature pine flatwoods, hydric pine flatwoods, depressional marsh wetlands, dry prairie and permanent freshwater ponds. A variety of birds are abundant including several species of wading birds, great horned owls and bald eagles. A diversity of reptiles and amphibians can be observed in and around the wetlands; bobcats, otters and deer can also be observed within the park. Timber thinning of primarily slash pines pines due to fire suppression, before prescribed fire can be implemented.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Amberjack Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project focused on removing slash pines from fire dependant natural communities to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species. The timber thinning was done by Conservation Charlotte staff.
Habitat_Description: The Amberjack Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. Amberjack Environmental Park includes 225 acres of unique scrub, pine flatwoods, marshes and other beautiful areas, traversed by two significant wetlands. They are haven for several species of wading birds, including glossy ibis, roseate spoonbills and snowy egrets. Two boardwalk lead to observational platforms on Lemon Lake, where people can enjoy the amazing variety of birds who inhabit the lake and the surrounding areas.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Lamb of God Florida Native Plantings
Project_Description: The Lamb of God Florida Native Planting project activities focused on planting native flowers and grasses along the ditches and swales on site to filter water and run-off before it reaches Estero Bay tributaries. The project is adjacent to and expands a previously planted butterfly garden of native wildflowers. Educational signs were placed at the site.
Habitat_Description: The Lamb of God Florida Native Plantings project is located in Fort Myers in Lee County and the parcel is primarily disturbed grass sod with ditches and swales.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Yucca Pens Preserve Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive  exotic vegetation, primarily Brazilian pepper Melaleuca. Ongoing projects include: installation of fencing & fire lines, pine tree thinning, and mowing/disking perimeter fire breaks. Future plans will include staff performing prescribed burns within fire dependant plant communities.
Habitat_Description: The Yucca Pens Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in northwest Lee County. The preserve is approximately 234 acres in size and parts are  adjacent of Babcock-Webb Wildlife Management Area. The preserve consists of twelve plant communities; one-third which are highly impacted from past uses. Historically, portions of the Preserve were used for agriculture and illegally as a site for outdoor recreation (camping, shooting/hunting and off-road activities). Ditches, berms, furrows, borrow and spoil areas, off-road vehicles (ORV), as well as invasive exotic plants have disturbed many portions of the wetland and upland plant communities. The dominant plant communities found on the preserve are mixed mesic (flatwoods and hammock), mesic flatwoods and wet flatwoods. The preserve contains a combination of wetland and upland communities that serve as important habitat for a variety of birds, mammals, reptiles and amphibians.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Manatee Elementary Class Rain Gutter Wetland Project
Project_Description: The Manatee Elementary Class Rain Gutter Wetland project activities focused on directing rain runoff to a created wetland water retention area and developing materials for creating "at home" wetland ecosystems and their values.
Habitat_Description: The Manatee Elementary Class Rain Gutter Wetland Project is located in Fort Myers in Lee County an a school parcel that is primarily disturbed grass sod with some native oaks surrounded by residential and open lands.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Corkscrew Regional Ecosystem Watershed Preserve Acquisition
Project_Description: The Corkscrew Regional Ecosystem Watershed Preserve project focused on acquisition of lands for preservation and restoration of cypress and other forested wetlands adjacent to existing preserves.
Habitat_Description: The Corkscrew Regional Ecosystem Watershed Preserve is a Lee County Conservation 2020 acquisition located in Lee County adjacent to the Pine Lake Conservation Preserve and the Corkscrew Regional Ecosystem Watershed. The primary habitats includes forested wetlands and cypress, which provide aquifer recharge, natural flood protection and water purification, and support such wildlife as the Florida panther and black bear.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Caloosahatchee Creeks Preserve Restoration 2010 project focuses on prescribed fire and removal of invasive exotic animals (over 50 wild hogs were trapped).
Habitat_Description: The Caloosahatchee Creeks Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County along the Caloosahatchee River, bisected by Interstate 75. The preserve is 1290 acres in size and the eastern side, includes pine flatwoods and hammock, and the western side includes a canoe and kayak launch into Popash Creek. Primary habitats include tidal wetlands, mangrove swamps and mesic pine flatwoods.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserved Restoration project focused on treating invasive exotic vegetation, primarily Melaleuca.
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve Restoration project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County, adjacent to the Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park. The Preserve contains 400 acres of several plant communities including pine flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods, scrub, oak hammock, tidal salt flats, tidal marsh, tidal swamps, and a disturbed Australian pine monoculture.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Ramblers Rest Campground Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010
Project_Description: The Ramblers Rest Campground Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project focused on treating Brazilian pepper using chainsaws and cut stump herbicide applications. The Brazilian pepper is chipped on site once it is cut, using Ramblers Rest equipment. The project is expected to continue into the future.
Habitat_Description: The Ramblers Rest Campground Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 Project is located in Charlotte County and managed through the Myakka Wild and Scenic River Management Program. The primary habitat is disturbed forested wetlands and riverine floodplain heavily infested with Brazilian pepper with some native live oaks and cabbage palms intermixed. The area where Brazilian pepper has been removed consists of native wetland species including saltbush and some leather fern.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Oyster Creek Regional Park Timber Thinning 2010
Project_Description: The Oyster Creek Regional Park Timber Thinning 2010 project focused on removing slash pines from fire dependant natural communities to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species. The timber thinning was done by Conservation Charlotte staff.
Habitat_Description: The Oyster Creek Regional Park Timber Thinning 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. The park has over 420 acres and is a sanctuary of old growth pines, scrub habitat and mature pine flatwoods with mangrove fringe along Oyster Creek. An observation platform and the boardwalk crossing Oyster Creek displays the variety of birds that utilize Oyster Creek and the surrounding mangroves.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Timber Harvest 2010
Project_Description: The Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Timber Harvest 2010 project focused on removing sand pines from fire dependant natural communities to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species, including longleaf pines. The timber harvest was done under a contract administered by the Florida Division of Forestry. Proceeds from the timber sale go toward restoration activities at the park.
Habitat_Description: The Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Timber Harvest 2010 project is located in Manatee County, managed by the Florida Parks Service. The primary habitats include scrub, scrubby flatwoods, mesic flatwoods and sandhill, as well as an over abundance of sand pines due to fire suppression.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Galt Preserve Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive exotic vegetation, primarily Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca. Future projects include nature trails that allow visiters to see the different exotic plant control techniques and restored native plant communities, a map of the trails, and a fishing pier and picnic tables adjacent to the borrow pond.
Habitat_Description: The Galt Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County on Pine Island. The preserve totals 265 acres contains twelve plant communities including tidal swamps, mesic flatwoods, melaleuca monocultures, mixed exotics, borrow ponds, and tidal marshes. The preserve is home to variety of animal species, mainly wading birds, including white ibis, snowy egrets, little blue herons and American alligators.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Fisherman's Wharf Condominium Association Native Plant Restoration
Project_Description: The Fisherman's Wharf Condominium Association completed this 3rd phase of restoring native plants on their association property. They removed non-native vegetation and created native vegetation and flower gardens alongside the buildings and canal. They planted native coonties, ferns and lantana and used Flora Mulch to finish the beds. They also explain the value of native vegetation to homeowners.
Habitat_Description: The Fisherman's Wharf Condominium Association Native Plant Restoration project is located in Saint James City in Lee County and the residential parcel has a mixed habitat of disturbed grass sod and pine flatwoods.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Boys and Girls Club Butterfly Garden was created by removing the grass sod; adding soil, topsoil, peat moss and compost; removing non-indigenous vegetation; planting native wildflowers attractive to butterflies; and adding mulch.
Habitat_Description: The Boys and Girls Club Butterfly Garden project is located in Port Charlotte in Lee County and was created on a residential lot primarily grass sod vegetation.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Shell Creek Preserve Roller Chopping 2010 project focused on roller chopping vegetation in fire dependant natural communities, primarily pine flatwoods, to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species. The roller chopping was done by Conservation Charlotte staff.
Habitat_Description: The Shell Creek Preserve Roller Shopping 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. Shell Creek Preserve is a 370 acres preserve consisting of cypress lined creek banks, xeric hammock, small areas of mesic hammock, scrub, depressional marshes and large areas of longleaf pine dominated mesic flatwoods. Shell Creek preserve provides visitors the opportunity to observe the birds and wildlife while canoeing on the creek that runs through the center of the park.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Myakka Wild and Scenic River Program has been treating Brazilian pepper at this site for over 3 years through basal bark and girdling herbicide applications. Approximately 6 acres was treated this FY. No native vegetation has been replanted where the Brazilian pepper has been removed because the native vegetation recruits successfully on it's own. The exotic invasive vegetation treatment will continue until complete in 2011.
Habitat_Description: The Venice Campground Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project is located in Charlotte County and managed through the Myakka River Wild and Scenic River Management Program. The primary habitats include bottom-land swamp and riverine floodplain with hardwood wetland trees including pop ash, elm, maple, leather fern, as well as some invasive exotic Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Mullock Creek Preserve Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive exotic  vegetation, including Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper. In addition, Lee County Natural Resources will be performing hydrological restoration work in this area and will be incorporating some of the preserve's areas into their plans.
Habitat_Description: The Mullock Creek Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve is a 4 acre parcel adjacent to a south branching tributary of Mullock Creek. The preserve contains seven plant communities including wetland forested mixed, temperate hardwood, xeric oak, pine-mesic oak, exotic wetland hardwood, disturbed lands, and a portion of the creek's tributary. The drier xeric oak community is home to a small population of state-listed gopher tortoises, while a small American alligator was noted along the flowing creek.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Additions 2010
Project_Description: The Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Additions 2010 project focused on acquisition of 3 new parcels for preservation and restoration of cypress and other forested wetlands adjacent to the existing preserve.
Habitat_Description: The Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve Additions for 2010 project includes the addition of 3 parcels adjacent to the existing preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of cypress slough and forested wetlands. There is some exotic invasive vegetation (primarily Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper) and animals (primarily wild hogs).
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Cape Coral Urban Forestry by Rotary
Project_Description: The Cape Coral Urban Forestry by Rotary project activities focused on planting 2,000 native plants, including bald cypress and slash pines along Veteran's Memorial Parkway.
Habitat_Description: The Cape Coral Urban Forestry By Rotary Project is located in Cape Coral in Lee County. The primary habitat is disturbed grass sod in road right of way.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Bonita Springs Nature Place project activities focused on land acquisition, restoration of a residential house into a nature center, restoring native vegetation and gopher tortoise habitat, and adding a beehive, bat house, bird feeders and educational signs.
Habitat_Description: The Bonita Springs Nature Place is located in Bonita Springs in Lee County. The primary habitat is forested uplands and wetlands, with some freshwater wetlands adjacent to the Imperial River.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Hidden Cypress Preserve project focused on acquisition of lands for preservation and restoration of cypress and other forested wetlands and reconnection of surface water streams.
Habitat_Description: The Hidden Cypress Preserve is a Lee County Conservation 2020 acquisition located in Lee County within the County's Density Reduction/Groundwater Resource Area. The primary habitats include forested wetlands and cypress, which provide aquifer recharge, natural flood protection and water purification. The parcel reconnects Spring Creek to Lightner Creek and the Imperial River.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Pine Island Library Landscaping project focused on removal of non-native invasive vegetation, including Java Plums and planting of native vegetation including 3 live oaks, 100 slash pines and other native trees and shrubs and 1,500 wildflowers, butterfly nectar and host plants and ground cover plants. Crushed shell paths were put in place to create an "outdoor classroom" area.
Habitat_Description: The Pine Island Library Landscaping project is located on Pine Island in Lee County. The primary habitat was disturbed grass sod with non-native, invasive & non-invasive vegetation including Java Plum and fig trees.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Harbour Heights Native Plantings focussed on removing grass sod and planting native live oaks, buttonwoods, firebus, wax myrtles and sunshine mimosas.
Habitat_Description: The Harbour Heights Native Plantings project is located at the Sunny Brook Motel in Harbour Heights in Charlotte County and the property is primarily disturbed grass sod with some native slash pine trees.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral Restoration 2010
Project_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral Restoration 2010 project focused on removal and treatment of invasive exotic vegetation, primarily Australian pines and Brazilian pepper, and endangered species monitoring, supported by Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and Florida Parks Service
Habitat_Description: The Charlotte Harbor Preserve State Park Cape Coral Restoration 2010 project is located in Lee County and is managed by the Florida Parks Service. The primary habitats include native and disturbed mesic pine, mangrove swamps and riparian tidal creeks.
Main_Funding_Source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Pop Ash Creek Preserve Restoration 2010  project focused on treating invasive exotic  vegetation, including cogongrass, Melaleuca, Ceasarweed, Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca.
Habitat_Description: The Pop Ash Creek Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve is a 307 acre parcel, which contains both human-altered and natural plant communities that are mostly wet or mesic flatwoods and a portion of a blackwater stream (Popash Creek). Along the northern portion of Popash Creek, which was previously dredged, a lone pop ash tree (Fraxinus caroliniana) survives adjacent to larger Carolina willow (Salix caroliniana) and Brazilian pepper (Schinus terebinthifolius) trees. Past land uses and hydrologic modifications have disturbed about 90% of the Preserve.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Prescribed Fire 2010
Project_Description: The Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Prescribed Fire 2010 project focused on prescribed fire of scrub to benefit federally listed Florida Bonamia, as well as other fire dependant habitats. The project included assistance from Myakka City Volunteer Fire Station.
Habitat_Description: The Wingate Creek Preserve State Park Prescribed Fire 2010 project is located in Manatee County, managed by the Florida Parks Service. The primary habitats include scrub, mesic flatwoods, wet flatwoods and wet prairies, including the federally listed Florida Bonamia (an endemic scrub morning-glory).
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Alva Scrub Preserve Restoration 2010 project currently has active cattle leases in the pasture areas which are used as a management tool on this Preserve. This years activities focused on removal of invasive exotic plant treatment, including Lygodium (in cypress domes) and Brazilian pepper. Ongoing and future activities include pine tree thinning to improve habitat for the Federally listed Florida scrub jays which reside on the Preserve, roller chopping of palmetto, prescribed burning and planting of scrub jay forage species.
Habitat_Description: The Alva Scrub Preserve Restoration 2010 project is a Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve located in Lee County. The preserve is about 846 acres and contains a diversity of plant communities including mesic & scrubby flatwoods, oak hammock, wet prairie, floodplain swamp, unimproved pasture, cypress head and pond. These wetland areas provide feeding and roosting areas for numerous listed wading bird species, as well as many other animals. At this time, the Preserve has active cattle leases in the pasture areas which are used for management.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Longino Ranch Conservation Easement project focuses on purchasing the development rights from the agricultural parcel to preserve and restore native forested upland and wetland habitats.
Habitat_Description: The Longino Ranch Conservation Easement project is located in eastern Sarasota County between the Myakka and Peace Rivers. The parcel includes 3,890 acres of forested uplands, wetlands, range and pasture land, as well as some row crop and sod agriculture.
Main_Funding_Source: South West Florida Water Management District
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: San Carlos Bay Bunche Beach Preserve Restoration
Project_Description: The San Carlos Bay-Bunche Beach Preserve "Green" Activities Center Project focuses on invasive exotic vegetation removal, as well as providing composting toilets, roof top rainwater collectors, solar-powered electricity, kayak launches, fishing piers and additional parking developed on a disturbed spoil site instead of on the beach and mangrove vegetation.
Habitat_Description: The San Carlos Bay Bunche Beach Preserve "Green" Activities Center project is located in Fort Myers in Lee County. The primary habitats are mangrove swamp, tidal wetlands and coastal beach, with some invasive exotic vegetation, primarily Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Bonita Springs Gopher Tortoise Preserve and Butterfly Garden
Project_Description: The Bonita Springs Gopher Tortoise Preserve and Butterfly Garden activities included developing a beach shell walking path, preserving land for gopher tortoise, establishing a butterfly garden with native flowers and installing a bat house display, as well as educational signs.
Habitat_Description: The Bonita Spring Gopher Tortoise Preserve and Butterfly Garden is located in the City of Bonita Springs in Lee Count and was created on a disturbed, grass sodded parcel adjacent to a city park. Sod was replaced with native vegetation and land area was set aside for gopher tortoise habitat re-establishment.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Amberjack Environmental Park Prescribed Fire 2010 project focused on prescribed fire on 10 acres of pine flatwoods, scrub and wetlands to benefit native fire dependant habitats.
Habitat_Description: The Amberjack Environmental Park Prescribed Fire 2010 is located in Charlotte County. Amberjack Environmental Park includes 225 acres of unique scrub, pine flatwoods, marshes and other beautiful areas, traversed by two significant wetlands. They are havens for several species of wading birds, including glossy ibis, roseate spoonbills and snowy egrets. Two boardwalks lead to observational platforms on Lemon Lake, where people can enjoy the amazing variety of birds who inhabit the lake and the surrounding areas.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Prairie Creek Preserve Prescribed Fire 2010 project focused on prescribed fire on 350 acres of pine flatwoods, scrub and wetlands to benefit native fire dependant habitats.
Habitat_Description: The Prairie Creek Preserve Prescribed Fire 2010 Park Prescribed Fire 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. The preserve is a 1,600 acre preserve located on Prairie Creek, a tributary of Shell Creek Reservoir, which traverses through the center of the preserve providing open water foraging for wading birds and osprey. The diversity of habitats on the preserve varies from scrub, scrubby flatwoods, palmetto prairies, pine flatwoods, small areas of herbaceous marshes. The variety of habitats provides ample opportunities to observe several species of Florida wildlife, including the Florida scrub-jay, gopher tortoise, bobcats, deer and different species of reptiles and amphibians.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Thornton Key Preserve Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010
Project_Description: The Thornton Key Preserve Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project focused on treating primarily Brazilian pepper girdling and herbicide applications. Approximately 13 acres was treated this FY. No native vegetation has been replanted where the Brazilian pepper has been removed because the native vegetation recruits successfully on it's own.
Habitat_Description: The Thornton Key Preserve Exotic Vegetation Removal 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. Thornton Key is a barrier island in Lemon Bay south of Stump Pass and east of Palm Island; the Preserve is 31 acres in the center portion of the island. Thornton Key Preserve contains tropical coastal hammock, mangrove swamps, salt barrens, and herbaceous marsh. Tropical hardwood hammocks are home to numerous species of rare plants and are an important habitat for migratory birds. Looking over the salt barrens and marshes wading birds can be observed foraging and occasionally dolphins can be seen swimming out in Lemon Bay.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Cedar Point Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010
Project_Description: The Cedar Pint Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project focused on removing slash pines from fire dependant natural communities to allow the reintroduction of prescribed fire to restore habitats for listed and other native species. The timber thinning was done by Conservation Charlotte staff.
Habitat_Description: The Cedar Point Environmental Park Timber Thinning 2010 project is located in Charlotte County. With 115 acres, Cedar Point is one of Charlotte County's unique parks with pine flatwoods, salt marsh, mangrove fringe and hammock areas. Situated on Lemon Bay, a long, narrow estuary, Cedar Point is a great place to see beautiful wading birds that visit the mangrove fringe and adjacent seagrasses. The pine flatwoods are home a pair of bald eagles, as well as gopher tortoises and a myriad of native plants.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: The Telegraph Creek Prescribed Fire 2010 project focused on prescribed fire on 230 acres of pine flatwoods, scrub and wetlands to benefit native fire dependant habitats.
Habitat_Description: The Telegraph Creek Preserve Prescribed Fire 2010 project is located in Lee County and is a  Lee County Conservation 2020 preserve of about 1730 acres in size, including both sides of Telegraph Creek. The preserve includes a fairly large area of scrub as well as an almost 500-acre palmetto prairie that was maintained with fire by the previous land owners. Historically, Florida scrub jays (a Federally Threatened species) have been documented using the Preserve and restoration plans will partially focus on making the scrub suitable habitat for their return. These plans will also benefit the gopher tortoise (a state Threatened species) that is commonly found throughout drier portions of the Preserve. The preserve is interconnect to the 5620-acre Bob Janes Preserve and 67,619-acre Babcock Ranch Preserve in Charlotte County. Together, these conservation areas provide habitat for numerous listed species including the Florida black bear, Florida panther, crested caracara, red-cockaded woodpecker, eastern indigo snake, and Florida burrowing owl.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Community Based Oyster Restoration in Estero Bay
Project_Description: The Community Based Oyster Restoration in Estero Bay project focused on deployment of oyster shell substrate to enhance natural oyster recruitment in a lagoonal estuary. The project involved many partners and citizen volunteers and provided significant public education and  community involvement.
Habitat_Description: The Community Based Oyster Restoration in Estero Bay project is located in Lee County in a lagoonal estuary. The primary habitats are seagrass, unvegetated mudflats, mangroves and oysters. The oyster restoration sites provide settling areas for juvenile oyster spat. The oyster restoration project is a partnership between Florida Gulf Coast University and community volunteers.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that includes  invasive exotic vegetation removal of lygodium, restoring fire lines, planting donated pines and securing rezoning to Environmentally Critical status.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 3137 acre Wild Turkey Strand Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of flatwoods, cypress strand swamps, cypress dome swamps, freshwater marshes and wet prairies, as well as abandoned pastures. Extensive infestations of invasive exotic vegetation (primarily Melaleuca) are found throughout the preserve. Habitat diversity is diminished by lack of fire, though there are areas damaged from an intense wildfire in 2007. The preserve is located between the international airport and urban development, with altered hydrology within the preserve and from the adjacent watershed, including groundwater wells just to the south of the preserve. The preserve is located within Lee Counties density reduction/groundwater recharge area..
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Invasive exotic vegetation (Lygodium, tropical soda apple, cogongrass and Brazilian pepper) was removed, and roller chopping done in preparation for prescribed fire. A cooperative Scrub Jay mitigation plan is being developed and Scrub Jay and Gopher Tortoise habitat restoration activitites have been started.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 846 acre Alva Scrub Preserve Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of a diversity of plant communities including mesic and scrubby flatwoods, oak hammock, wet prairie, floodplain swamp, cypress head and ponds, as well as invasive exotic vegetation including cogongrass, Lygodium, tropical soda apple, Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca. Areas of the preserve are also in unimproved pasture use with active cattle leases. The native habitats rpovide feeding and roosting areas for numerous listed wading bird species, Scrub Jays, Gopher Tortoise and other animal species. Habitat diversity is decreased by lack of burning. this is a test
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat restoration project that includes invasive exotic vegetation removal of Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca, and Scrub Jay and Gopher Tortoise habitat enhancement. In addition, preparation was done for prescribed fire through roller chopping palmetto and installing fire lines.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 1,730 acre Telegraph Creek Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020  comprised of a variety of critical upland and wetland habitats which include scrub and palmetto prairie and riverine wetlands along Telegraph Creek. There is some invasive exotic vegetation (Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca)and habitat diversity is reduced due to lack of burning, but the native habitats support a great variety of animal species, including the listed Scrub Jay, Gopher Tortoise, black bear, Florida panther, crested caracara, red-cockaded woodpecker, eastern indigo snake and burrowing owls.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Habitat diversity is decreased by lack of burning. A prescribed fire was done on 200 acres.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing Carlton Reserve managed by Sarasota County County comprised of a diversity of plant communities including pine palmetto flatwoods, oak hammock, and freshwater wetlands, with some invasive exotic vegetation.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project including off-road vehicle trail restoration and exotic vegetation removal by Lee County staff and volunteers. In addition, over 150 feral hogs were removed.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 2,654 acre Prairie Pines Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of a mosaic of several native plant communities, including wet and mesic flatwoods, depression marshes, wet prairies, prairie hammocks and a small baygall, with some areas disturbed by illegal off-road vehicles and past agricultural practices. There are extensive invasive exotic plants including cogongrass, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper, as well as feral hogs.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a new land acquisition for protection and restoration of and public access to coastal uplands and mangroves which is purchased, managed and restored by the non-profit Calusa Land Trust and it's volunteers.
Habitat_Description: This is a new 51 acre Inman Preserve acquisition managed by the Calusa Land Trust, comprised of a mangrove fringe surrounding disturbed and filled uplands infested with extensive exotic vegetation including Australian pines, Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that includes removal of infestations of invasive exotic Australian Pines, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper through cutting and herbicide treatments and grading of previous agriculture lands to restore hydrology and natural flows.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic  restoration at the existing 272 acre Deep Lagoon Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of tidal swamps and marshes, coastal grasslands, wet prairies and prairie hammocks and mesic flatwoods, as well as pasture and old gladiolus agriculture fields. There are extensive invasive exotic plant mono-cultures of Australian pines, Brazilian pepper and melaleuca and hydrologic alterations within and into the preserve, which is surrounded by urbanized development. The native habitats support a variety of other plant and animal species, including several listed species, including the Smalltooth Sawfish. The preserve is in several parcels with a small area along the Caloosahatchee River.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This project is a new acquisition for protection and restoration and public access to tidal wetlands and mangroves managed and restored by the non-profit Calusa Land Trust and  it's volunteers.
Habitat_Description: This is a new 43 acre acquisition managed by the Calusa Land Trust, comprised primarily of tidal wetlands and mangroves with a small access point of disturbed uplands with extensive exotic vegetation including Australian pines, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This project is a new acquisition for protection and restoration and public  access of mesic pine flatwoods, tidal wetlands and mangroves, adjacent to an  existing preserve managed and restored by the non-profit Calusa Land Trust and  it's volunteers.
Habitat_Description: This is a new 10 acre acquisition managed by the Calusa Land Trust comprised primarily of tidal wetlands and mangroves, with some mesic pine flatwoods and native coastal uplands and disturbed uplands with extensive exotic vegetation including Australian pines, and Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Exotic vegetation Melaleuca was removed, and prescribed fire on 3 sites within the 400 acre preserve. Restoration of sheet flow.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 400 acre Charlotte Harbor Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of pine flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods, scrub, oak hammock, tidal salt flats, tidal marsh, tidal swamp. There is widely distributed exotic vegetation including Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that removed invasive exotic vegetation of downy rose myrtle, ear leaf acacia, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper, as well as blocking and restoring off-road vehicle trails.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 231 acre Yucca Pens Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of 12 plant communities including mixed mesic flatwoods and hammock, mesic and wet flatwoods with both wetland and upland communities that serve as important habitat for a variety of birds, mammals, reptiles and amphibians. Areas of the preserve were historically used for agriculture and illegal recreation (off-road vehicles) and there are ditches, dikes, berms, borrow and spoil areas, as well as extensive invasive exotic vegetation including downy rose myrtle, earleaf acacia, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is an acquisition/donation project for habitat protection and restoration and environmental education and recreation with future enhancement through implementation of a conceptual plan to remove exotic vegetation and develop low impact recreational improvements and parking.
Habitat_Description: This project is acquisition/donation of the 82 acre Culverhouse Nature Park conservation easement given to Sarasota County from Palmer Ranch Holdings. The parcel includes native upland and wetland habitats comprised of mesic hammock, pine flatwoods, freshwater wetlands, a pasture with a limited number of cattle, bahiagrass, scattered invasive exotic vegetation (Brazilian pepper), an artificially dug pond and an eagle nest. The parcel is to be set aside for preservation and protection and outdoor recreation and education opportunities consistent with conservation purposes. The park is surrounded by residential development and is located at the beginning of the Legacy Trail used for biking and walking.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Invasive exotic vegetation (cogongrass, Guinea grass, Lygodium, Wedelia, air potato and Brazilian pepper) was removed by agency staff and volunteers.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 1,290 acre Caloosahatchee Creeks Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of a complex variety of upland and wetland habitats in several parcels along the north side of the Caloosahatchee River east and west of I-75. The habitats include oak hammocks, pine flatwoods and mangroves, with extensive areas of exotic vegetation including cogongrass, Guinea grass, Lygodium, Wedelia, air potato and Brazilian pepper. The preserve includes developed public access with parking, restrooms, picnic pavilions, boardwalk, trails and canoe launch, which are frequently used. The native habitats support a great diversity of birds, mammals, fish and amphibians.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Peace Creek Clear Springs Blueberry FARMS Restoration
Project_Description: This is a riverine and depressional freshwater wetland restoration project accomplished through restoration of water quantity, timing and quality flowing into the wetlands from adjacent blueberry row crops. Agricultural best management practices on the adjacent blueberry row crops are being installed through the Facilitating Agricultural Resource  Management Systems (FARMS) program to reduce irrigation water needs and provide  alternative water supplies and improved irrigation techniques for blueberry agriculture. The project reduces reliance on mineralized groundwater (and mineralized subsequent runoff) by construction and operation of a 10 acre surface water irrigation reservoir and the necessary pumps, water filtration systems and wind machines.
Habitat_Description: This project is a riverine and depressional freshwater wetland restoration project adjacent to Peace Creek, a headwater tributary to the Peace River in Polk County. The habitat includes forested wetlands which have been extensively altered and reduced in quality and quantity due to alterations in quantity, timing and quality of overland flow from the adjacent agricultural fields at the Clear Springs Blueberry row crops.
Restoration_Technique: Stormwater/Runoff Controls (only choose for natural habitat)
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Six Mile Cypress Preserve North Restoration
Project_Description: Exotic invasive vegetation of Brazilian pepper and Australian pines was removed, and well as grading old ag lands to restore natural elevation and hydrology.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 750 acre Six Mile Cypress North Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of pine flatwoods, oak hammocks, cypress sloughs, riverine wetlands and abandoned and historic headwaters of the Six Mile Cypress Slough. The native uplands, wetlands and agricultural lands include invasive exotic vegetation and have altered hydrology within and into the preserve.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: Invasive exotic vegetation (Melaleuca, Brazilian pepper and others) was removed, fire lines were installed, prescribed fire was conducted, fences repaired, trash was removed, and disposed of an old tar pot. A Land Management Plan is currently being developed for the preserve.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 572 acre Buckingham Trails Preserve Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of highly disturbed habitats including scrub habitats and freshwater wetlands infested with Melaleuca, cattle pasture and a former army airfield and base with bunkers and jeep tracks used for target practice.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is an acquisition/donation project designed to accomplish habitat protection and restoration and public access with the addition of invasive exotic vegetation and litter removal activities conducted by the non-profit Calusa Land Trust and it's volunteers in the future.
Habitat_Description: This project is acquisition/donation of the 8 acre Flanagan Preserve to the Calusa Land Trust for preservation, restoration and public access. The parcel is located on an unbridged barrier island adjacent to residential development and is comprised of beach, coastal dune, tidal wetlands and mangroves, with some invasive exotic vegetation (Australian pines and Brazilian pepper).
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This project is a new acquisition for restoration of mesic pine flatwoods, tidal wetlands and mangroves.
Habitat_Description: This is a new addition adjacent to the existing 540 acre Pine Island Flatwoods Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of pasture and disturbed uplands and freshwater wetlands with some intact mangroves and saltmarsh. There is extensive exotic vegetation including Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: Daniels Preserve at Spanish Creek Restoration
Project_Description: This is a habitat restoration project that includes preparation for prescribed fire and removal of invasive exotic vegetation.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 243 acre Daniels Preserve at Spanish Creek Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of 21 plant communities and the headwaters of Spanish Creek. The dominant plant communities are pine flatwoods, oak hammocks, wetlands forested mixed, and pine-mesic oak, along with improved pasture that is still in an active cattle lease. There are areas of invasive exotic vegetation including Brazilian pepper and cogongrass. The native habitats support a diversity of animal species, including the listed Gopher Tortoise.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat restoration project that includes invasive exotic vegetation  removal of Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper, as well roller chopping overgrown areas of saw palmetto. Plans are being considered to build a boardwalk for manatee viewing.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 59 acre Orange River Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of three plant communities including scrubby flatwoods, mesic hammock and tidal swamp, including three species of mangroves, and apples and leather fern. There is also extensive invasive exotic vegetation including Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper. The preserve consists of 3 parcels adjacent to the Orange River divided by a private out parcel.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that includes invasive exotic vegetation  removal of ear leaf acacia, cogongrass, Guinea grass Caesar weed, Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper plus a major hydrologic restoration project has been initiated to correct historic sheet flow into the preserve, connect artificial ponds and reduce flooding in the adjacent neighborhoods.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 307 acre Pop Ash Creek Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of wet and mesic flatwood and riverine wetlands, as well as invasive exotic vegetation including ear leaf acacia, cogongrass, Carolina Willow, Brazilian pepper and Melaleuca. The hydrology within and draining to the preserve has been extensively altered, affecting 90% of the preserve.
Restoration_Technique: Stormwater/Runoff Controls (only choose for natural habitat)
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Name: San Carlos Bay Bunche Beach Preserve Restoration
Project_Description: This is a habitat restoration project that includes removal of invasive exotic vegetation and litter by bird patrols and by staff and volunteers. The preserve also provides environmental education opportunities and is used by FL Gulf Coast University, Edison College and Lee County Schools, as well as volunteer guided public walks, as an outdoor classroom.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 704 acre San Carlos Bay Bunche Beach Preserve Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of a variety of coastal habitats including tidal swamp, tidal creeks, coastal grasslands, coastal berms, mudflats and seagrass beds which support a wide variety of animal, fish and bird species. The preserve offers excellent environmental education and recreational opportunities and high access with low impact parking and restroom facilities.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat restoration project that focuses on removal of exotic vegetation, including Melaleuca, Brazilian pepper, and earleaf acacia. There are plans for trails, boardwalk and observation deck.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat restoration at the existing 265 acre Galt Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of twelve plant communities including tidal swamps, mesic flatwoods, melaleuca mono-cultures, mixed exotics, borrow ponds, and tidal marshes which are home to variety of animal species, mainly wading birds, including white ibis, snowy egrets, little blue herons and American alligators.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that includes invasive exotic vegetation  removal (Melaleuca and Brazilian pepper) as well as restoring disturbed trails, fire lines and altered hydrologic flows within and into the preserve.
Habitat_Description: This project includes habitat and hydrologic restoration at the existing 243 acre Estero Marsh Preserve managed by Lee County Conservation 2020 comprised of eight native plant communities including estuarine tidal swamp and marshes, mesic and wet flatwoods, mesic hammock, tidal swamp lake, brackish marshes and tidal salt tern, with some previously cleared lands, old trails, electrical power transmission lines and invasive exotic vegetation. There is also some hydrologic disturbance from dikes, berms and levees. The preserve is adjacent to both urban development as well as the Estero Bay Preserve State Park.
NEP_Name: Coastal and Heartland National Estuary Partnership

Project_Description: This is a habitat and hydrologic restoration project that includes restoration of natural and sheet flow within the preserve, as well as stormwater management within immediate watershed. There is some limited invasive exotic plant removal on this small parcel and plans include restoring, expanding and maintaining a nature trail.
