Project_Name: Brevard Zoo North Indian River Lagoon Oyster Project 2
Project_Description: Brevard Zoo constructed a total of 4,871 square feet of oyster reef in various locations throughout the North Indian River Lagoon. The contract is for a total of 21,030 square feet, of which 3,490 was constructed this year and 1,381 was constructed in previous years.
Habitat_Description: Estuary bottom near shoreline.

Project_Name: Reconnect Wetland CX-40 Cape Canaveral Air Force Station
Project_Description: Installation of two 42 inch culverts under Centaur Road to re-connect impounded wetlands to IRL system in North Banana River section of the Indian River Lagoon.
Habitat_Description: Impounded wetlands adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon.

Project_Description: This project used Florida Friendly landscaping principles to improve the Grassy Point Preserve. Participance incorporated native plants and signage for the public. The signs included plant identification information and a site map.
Habitat_Description: Grassy Point Preserve is a recently enhanced coastal habitat in the City of Holmes Beach on Anna Maria Island, Florida.

Project_Name: Promote Paradise and Remove A Parking Lot
Project_Description: Marine Discovery Center is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that operates on 22 acres of the former New Smyrna Beach high school along the Northern region of the Indian River Lagoon. Project objectives included removing one section of a large parking lot area and hardened Hydrotex material that was used as a barrier seawall. Over half an acre of impervious surfaces were removed to create a 1:6 slope, install three types of non-plastic wavebreaks, and plant native plants along the ecotone.
Habitat_Description: Hardened shoreline structure was replaced with living shoreline methods like non-plastic breakwaters, marsh grasses, mangroves, and upper ecotone plants. The project is not only successful in shoreline stabilization, but also offers accessibility for passive recreation through grass walking paths and a kayak launch. Overall, it also serves as a demonstration of how to implement native species to enhance both wetland and upland habitats.

Project_Name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge Exotic Plant Control - Air Potato 2013
Project_Description: Non-native invasive air potato plants were treated and killed in upland habitats of the refuge.
Habitat_Description: Coastal marsh, pine flatwoods, and scrub located within the Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge. The refuge is bounded by the Indian River Lagoon and Atlantic ocean.

Project_Description: Thirty-none volunteers planted native species, removed rosary pea plants and created portable "Stow-It-Don't-Throw-It" monofilament recycling containers at Emerson Point Preserve.
Habitat_Description: Emerson Point Preserve is a 365 acre preserve located at the tip of Snead Island in western Palmetto.At Emerson Point, visitors can take in the beauty of Florida's wildlife and native plant communities while exploring both prehistoric and historic sites. Historical resources include the Portavant Temple Mound, southwest Florida's largest Native American Temple Mound, and the surrounding midden complex. Multi-use trails and boardwalks are aligned so that the natural habitat and cultural resources will be protected. There is a large ten table picnic shelter and two small picnic shelters available for rental/reservation. A canoe/kayak launch allows access to the tidal canals and Terra Ceia Bay. A Welcome/Ranger Station is open Friday and Saturday for visitors.

Project_Name: Florida Institute of Saltwater Heritage (FISH) Preserve
Project_Description: A three acre section of the FISH Preserve was target for exotic vegetation removal. This section contained a dense stand of Australian pines. The cleared acreage will make way for a tidal wetland feature during the next phase of restoration.
Habitat_Description: The Florida Institute of Saltwater Heritage (FISH) is dedicated to preserving the cultural and environmental integrity of Florida's traditional maritime communities. In 2004, FISH acquired 95 acres of upland, mangrove wetland and submerged bay bottom in western Manatee County and named it the FISH Preserve. Although the Preserve has remained undeveloped, the uplands and wetlands have been impacted by mosquito ditching and land alterations leading to invasive trees dominating the upland areas. A long range restoration and management plan is required to reestablish native communities.

Project_Description: For this project phase, we improved hydrology of an existing coastal tidal creek by removing fallen and decaying Australian pines from the waterway. We also improved the adjacent upland coastal habitat by removing remaining Australian pines from project site. This project addressed the need for additional and improved wetland features (tidal creeks) for juvenile fish habitat and potential upland habitat features for gopher tortoises.
Habitat_Description: North Lido Park is located on Lido Key, Florida. The Park is contiguous to both the Gulf of Mexico and Sarasota Bay (Pansy Bayou), which provides multi-purpose passive recreational opportunities to the public. The Park is owned by the City of Sarasota, but managed by Sarasota County. The SBEP has conducted previous habitat improvements within the Park and continues to work with Sarasota County to restore other Park habitats and to improve hydrologic function of the wetland areas.
Main_Funding_Source: Southwest Florida Water Management District ($21,450), US Fish & Wildlife Service ($15,000)

Project_Description: This phase of work allowed for the removal of Australian pines from another (five acre) section of the Park (recently renamed Ted Sperling Park). This included the removal of several very large, mature pines that required special equipment for safely topping, sectioning and removing these trees.
Habitat_Description: South Lido Park is a 105-acre parcel on the southern portion of Lido Key in Sarasota County. Dredge and fill activities have disturbed the area and created ideal conditions for the invasion of exotic vegetation. The popular park boasts shorelines along the Gulf of Mexico, Big Pass and Sarasota Bay and contains several salt water lagoons. The waterways that wind through the Park are very popular with kayakers. Several nature trails also allow visitors a close-up experience with this valuable coastal habitat. Several previous habitat improvement projects have taken place within the Park. In 2005, exotic trees were removed from a 38-acre parcel and several tidal connections were created and/or improved. In 2007, another phase of work addressed similar issues at other locations within the Park. Both projects also included installing native wetland plants to stabilize the waterways.

Project_Description: Otter Key is a twenty-acre mangrove-dominated coastal island with an three acre upland interior. This interior section is covered with several species of invasive trees which greatly reduces the habitat quality for wading and shore birds and other wildlife that live on or frequent the island. Brazilian pepper, carrotwood trees, and Australian pines were cut and temporarily disposed on site, then mulched and removed where possible. Trimming to raise branches and under-brushing of trees and palms was also done. Tree stumps were treated with herbicide; nuisance ground cover, nuisance grasses and shrubs were also treated.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine mangrove island with three acres of overgrown coastal uplands.

Project_Name: Palma Sola Wetland Restoration at Robinson Preserve
Project_Description: This project removed Australian pines (exotic trees) from uplands within the Robinson Preserve that drain into Palma Sola Bay. Treatment consisted of cutting and mulching in place and grinding the stumps.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland with invasive exotic vegetation infiltration

Project_Description: Construction and deployment of a variety of artificial reef modules designed to provide estuarine habitat for juveniles of recreationally important fish, particularly gag grouper. Reef material was deployed at three Sarasota County reefs: Harts (26 modules), Walker (63 modules) and Anglers Reefs (21 modules). Reef modules consisted of deep cover, cubes, rings and a variety of reef balls.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine artificial reefs in Sarasota Bay

Project_Name: Sarasota Bay Oyster Habitat Creation: Manatee County
Project_Description: Two and a half acres of oyster habitat was created in 2011. This year, we added an additional 16 tons of loose shell to these reefs to account for settlement and sedimentation that reduced the overall vertical relief of the existing oyster beds.
Habitat_Description: Subtidal and intertidal oyster habitat

Project_Name: Invasive Plant Removal at Bay Walk Creek
Project_Description: A group of Bay Guardian volunteers with the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) completed an exotic vegetation project at Bay Walk Creek in February, 2013. Baywalk Creek is located near New College of Florida. The volunteers removed more than 1,000 pounds of the invasive air potato vine and tubers. The group also removed other non-native species.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland with natural estuarine shoreline.

Project_Description: 150 acres of coastal upland adjacent to the existing Robinson Preserve (484 acres) in Manatee County adjacent to Sarasota and Tampa Bays was acquired. Conceptual plans for habitat restoration of the site are being  prepared and funding sources to conduct the work are being identified.
Habitat_Description: Agricultural land, exotic tree forest and invasive vegetation.
Main_Funding_Source: Donation to Conservation Foundation of the Gulf Coast from the Mosaic Company Foundation

Project_Name: Bowlees Creek Island Invasive Species Removal
Project_Description: A group of 47 adult and student volunteers with the SBEP Bay Guardian Program removed debris and exotic plants on Bowlees Creek Island on Saturday. Bowlees Creek Island is a bird sanctuary located near the mouth of Bowlees Creek. The volunteers removed an estimated 427 pounds of debris and exotic plants. A picnic lunch for the volunteers was donated by local residents to support the project.
Habitat_Description: Bowlees Creek Island is a bird sanctuary located near the mouth of Bowlees Creek. Shoreline includes shellfish beds, tidal mudflats and intertidal seagrasses.

Project_Name: Bay Guardians Native Planting at Jiggs Landing
Project_Description: A group of 54 Bay Guardian volunteers with the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) planted more than 1,400 native plants at Jiggs Landing Preserve on Saturday, March 9. Jiggs Landing is located on the Ever’s Reservoir in Manatee County. The property was originally purchased in 1944; the popular fishing camp has undergone extensive renovations and was re-opened to the public in late 2010.
Habitat_Description: Jiggs Landing is located on the Ever’s Reservoir in Manatee County. The property was originally purchased in 1944; the popular fishing camp has undergone extensive renovations and was re-opened to the public in late 2010.

Project_Description: The Sarasota Bay Estuary Program and City of Sarasota partnered on this project to install a living shoreline along the bay at Bay Front Park in downtown Sarasota. The project featured 500 feet of native plants within the tidal zone to stabilize the sediments and provide intertidal habitat. The project was designed to showcase the natural beauty and benefits of these alternatives to more traditional hardened (sea walls) shorelines.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine shoreline planted with native tidal vegetation.

Project_Description: This project consisted of removing 2500 square feet of sterile turf covered landscape along a tidal estuary creek and replacing it with Florida native plants. The plants were carefully selected to thrive in the specific location and will never require pest control or fertilizer. Once established, watering will not be required. Initially, Melaleuca mulch was used to keep plants at the necessary moisture level. As the peanut plant (ground cover) matured, the mulch was no longer be needed and the watering system was turned off, only being used in cases of extreme drought. This planting along the creek provides cleaner run-off into the creek and estuary system while benefiting wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Retrofit an existing turf to a Florida friendly garden.

Project_Name: Palma Sola Scenic Highway Invasive Species Removal
Project_Description: This project continued the removal of invasive vegetation (Australian pine, Brazilian pepper and carrotwood trees) as well as dead palm trunks on bridges and right-of-way along the Palma Sola Scenic Highway. Doing so promoted awareness of sustainability, stormwater runoff, water conservation and the quality of Sarasota Bay.
Habitat_Description: Palma Sola Scenic Highway is 4.5 miles of SR 64 West/Manatee Avenue in Bradenton, Florida

Project_Description: A group of 38 volunteers with the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) Bay Guardians planted thousands of Florida native plants at Perico Preserve. Manatee County Natural Resources and Around the Bend Nature Tours supported the project. The plants, including cord grass, buttonwoods and sea grapes, were donated by the Florida Wildlife Commission and the Southeast Littoral Society.
Habitat_Description: The 176-acre property was originally farmland and the extensive mangrove fringe is currently undergoing restoration to become another natural habitat within Manatee County’s coastal preserve system.

Project_Description: Planting of native vegetation along the shoreline of Ever's Reservoir at Jiggs Landing. Sixty-eight volunteers helped plant a variety of freshwater wetland plants.
Habitat_Description: Parkland adjacent to Jigg's Landing on the Ever's Reservoir.

Project_Description: This  bay-education and bay-friendly landscaping project removed invasive and exotic plant species  from the current dry detention area on the New College campus. At the same time, students created a native, vegetated dry detention area in its place. Success was evaluated by monitoring native plant survival and development and attraction of insect and wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland native vegetated dry detention area.

Project_Name: Save Our Seabirds Native Planting Project
Project_Description: Bay-friendly native vegetation was planted and exotic and invasive plants throughout Save Our Seabirds (S.O.S.) Wild Bird Learning Center were removed. This project was intended to beautify the environment and enhance the educational experiences of visitors. Educational signage was installed, which emphasizes the importance of planting native vegetation to protect the environment and attract native birds, enhance the experience for over 25,000 visitors per year.
Habitat_Description: The open area of City Island consists ooastal meadow and grasslands.

Project_Description: This was a bay-friendly landscaping project to remove invasive plant species while incorporating native plant species. The site is a rookery used by many bird species. Kayakers, residents, and tourists come to view birds during nesting season.
Habitat_Description: Coastal peninsula serving as a bird rookery

Project_Description: The re-nourishment of a barrier island beach to for protection, recreation and habitat creation for shore birds. Approximately 265,000 cubic yards of sand was pumped onto eroded beaches from Bradenton Beach south to Longboat Pass.
Habitat_Description: Coastal beach along Sarasota Bay barrier island.

Project_Description: Creation of a sixteen acre bird rookery on abandoned agricultural lands through excavation and earth moving to form an island within a shallow estuarine pool. The island was planted with native trees and other vegetation for nesting/roosting birds.
Habitat_Description: Bird rookery created from abandoned agricultural lands.

Project_Description: The Parcel native habitats include Deer Prairie Creek and pristine pine flatwoods, hammock, depression marshes, dry prairie and scrub habitats. The pine flatwoods have a moderate fire fuel load.The Parcel native habitats include Deer Prairie Creek and pristine pine flatwoods, hammock, depression marshes, dry prairie and scrub habitats. The pine flatwoods have a moderate fire fuel load.
Habitat_Description: The Parcel native habitats include Deer Prairie Creek and pristine pine flatwoods, hammock, depression marshes, dry prairie and scrub habitats. The pine flatwoods have a moderate fire fuel load.

Project_Name: Tom Bennett Park Exotic Species Control
Project_Description: Treatment of fifteen acres of monotypic stand of Brazillian pepper. This was the first maintenance treatment for this park.
Habitat_Description: Upland parkland with several natural trails through freshwater wetlands and uplands.

Project_Name: Robinson Preserve Expansion- Reasoner Tract Exotics Removal
Project_Description: The treatment and removal of twenty acres of heavily infested Australian pines from the Reasoner tract within the Robinson Preserve (Manatee County).
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland and wetlands; former agricultural lands

Project_Description: Australian pines were removed and replaced with more than 400 native plants, including green buttonwood and sabal palms.
Habitat_Description: Coastal beach and dune system

Project_Description: Treatment and removal of twenty acres of exotic plants followed by planting native coastal vegetation.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine upland and wetland park

Project_Description: Forty two Bay Guardian volunteers removed invasive vegetation from 1.5 acres of the Preserve and planted native species.
Habitat_Description: Emerson Point is a coastal, estuarine preserve containing natural habitats

Project_Name: Oscar Sherer Park Habitat Restoration: Phase 1 (Lake Osprey)
Project_Description: Restoration of the littoral shelf and shoreline along half of the perimeter of Lake Osprey. Activities included excavation, grading and planting in four zones along the shore. The project provided access to the lake for park activities.
Habitat_Description: A large acreage of scrubby flatwoods that is home to several families of the Florida scrub-jays, a threatened species found only in Florida. The park protects scrubby and pine flatwoods that were once widespread throughout Sarasota County.

Project_Name: Oscar Sherer Park Habitat Restoration: Phase 3 (Big Lake)
Project_Description: Extensive shoreline and littoral zone excavation and re-grading, coupled with treatment of cattails in the shallow waters. The littoral zone modifications will prevent the rapid return of cattails along the banks of the lake.
Habitat_Description: A large acreage of scrubby flatwoods that is home to several families of the Florida scrub-jays, a threatened species found only in Florida. the park protects scrubby and pine flatwoods that were once widespread throughout Sarasota County.

Project_Description: Land acquisition consisting of hydric-mesic flatwoods, depressional wetlands, wet prairie and , mesic hammock.
Habitat_Description: Habitats include hydric-mesic flatwoods, depressional wetlands, wet prairie, mesic hammock and a borrow pit. This natural land provides nesting and foraging areas for wildlife, including bald eagle, swallow-tailed kite, sandhill crane, white-tailed deer, bobcat, otter and wading birds. Native plants include lopsided Indian, bluestem and wire grasses, along with goldenrod, black-eyed susan and Coreopsis, Florida’s State Wildflower. This buffer parcel within the Little Sarasota Bay watershed helps protect the water quality of that estuary system

Project_Description: Fifty-five volunteers with the Sarasota Bay Guardians removed air potato vines from native vegetation within Arlington Park.
Habitat_Description: Upland wooded park with numerous oak and pine trees.

Project_Name: Oscar Sherer Park Habitat Restoration: Phase 2 (Isolated Wetland)
Project_Description: Restoration of a historical freshwater wetland through exotic removal, re-grading and planting. This project also created several smaller frog ponds adjacent to the larger wetland.
Habitat_Description: A large acreage of scrubby flatwoods that is home to several families of the Florida scrub-jays, a threatened species found only in Florida. The park protects scrubby and pine flatwoods that were once widespread throughout Sarasota County.

Project_Description: Acquisition of 6.2 acres of undeveloped  property for inclusion into a watershed stormwater treatment system using low impact design.
Habitat_Description: Urban property consisting of an open field with pine trees and other vegetation.

Project_Name: South Lido Beach exotic vegetation removal
Project_Description: Australian pines at one time were widely planted in Florida to soak up the "swamps", stabilize canals and hold beaches. However, these fast growing trees provide dense shade and emit an herbicide that kills most any other plant that grow with the drip lines. Australian pines are on the Category 1 list of the most invasive plants according to the Florida Exotic Pest Plant Council (www.fleppc.org). The pines have a shallow root system. The wood is brittle and break under pressure and high winds such as hurricanes. The trees are also highly flammable. This project is the removal of several Australian pine stands within Ted Sperling (South Lido) Park.
Habitat_Description: Coastal park with extensive wetland and upland habitats

Project_Description: Treatment of exotic/invasive plants within Hidden Harbor utilizing chemical and physical treatments. Targeted species Include: cogon grass, Brazilian pepper, guinea grass, hairy indigo, and Australian pine trees.
Habitat_Description: Disturbed areas located within the Preserve boundaries

Project_Name: Robinson Preserve Estuarine Habitat Oyster Bar Creation
Project_Description: Placement of fossilized shell (in bags) as cultch  for future establishment of oyster bar habitat was conducted to  increase the oyster population in Sarasota Bay and at the same time, provide habitats for small organisms, +improve water quality and improve fish and wildlife habitats. Oyster larvae or spat attach to the shell and grow.
Habitat_Description: Intertidal to subtidal sand bottom

Project_Name: Perico Perimeter Berm Preserve Exotics Treatment
Project_Description: Treatment of exotic/invasive plants within Perico Preserve on perimeter berm utilizing chemical and physical treatments. Targeted species include: cogon grass, Brazilian pepper, guinea grass, hairy indigo, and Australian pine trees
Habitat_Description: Disturbed  areas located within the Preserve boundaries
Main_Funding_Source: All volunteer work; no funds required

Project_Description: Removal of a stand of fifteen mature Australian pine trees from this Sarasota County preserve. Tree trunks were used to mark nature trails.
Habitat_Description: North Lido Park is located on Lido Key, Florida. The Park is contiguous to both the Gulf of Mexico and Sarasota Bay (Pansy Bayou), which provides multi-purpose passive recreational opportunities to the public. The Park is owned by the City of Sarasota, but managed by Sarasota County. The SBEP has conducted previous habitat improvements within the Park and continues to work with Sarasota County to restore other Park habitats and to improve hydrologic function of the wetland areas.

Project_Description: The project created a bioswale at the Sarasota Aubudon Nature Center at the Celery Fields and  planted it with native trees, shrubs and plants. This collaboration project with Sarasota Audubon and the Florida House Institute educated local residents about stormwater pollution, native plants, water conservation, and the Phillippi Creek watershed. Interpretative signage was installed with the bioswale to enhance education.
Habitat_Description: Open uplands adjacent to County stormwater treatment area
Main_Funding_Source: US Environmental Protection Agency National Estuary Program

Project_Description: This project restored a portion of the shoreline on Phillippi Creek, which was eroded and filled with invasive plants (e.g. Brazilian pepper, cogan grass, etc.).The project activities involved further development of Riverview’s native plant trail through restoring approximately 75 feet of shoreline, removing invasive mahoe trees and replanting natives to reduce erosion. As part of the overall project and to develop community stewardship through awareness, a four foot wide 330 linear foot shell path with signage and habitat viewing areas was installed parallel to the improved shoreline and native plant trail.
Habitat_Description: Coastal tidal creek shoreline
Main_Funding_Source: US Environmental Protection Agency National Estuary Program

Project_Name: North Water Tower Park Exotic Removal
Project_Description: Extensive exotic removal was undertaken in both wetland and upland areas within this urban park. The work was done in advance of construction of an extensive stormwater treatment project that will incorporate many low impact design elements.
Habitat_Description: This is an urban park consisting of oak and pine hammocks

Project_Description: SBEP hosted a Bay Guardian volunteer event at G.T. Bray Park in Bradenton There were 48 volunteers who removed invasive species and trash. The volunteers removed approximately 1,500 Carrotwood trees from a bank near an athletic field. Other invasive species removed included Brazilian pepper, wandering jew, cherry laurel tree and Surinam cherry.
Habitat_Description: Urban park and recreational area
Main_Funding_Source: US Environmental Protection Agency National Estuary Program

Project_Description: More than 70 volunteers contributed to the air potato roundup. The volunteers collected 2,462 pounds of air potato. The air potato is an invasive vine that covers and shades beneficial native plants. The vine grows a large tuber that looks like a hanging potato. Volunteers enjoyed a picnic lunch following the project.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetlands and wooded parkland.
Main_Funding_Source: US Environmental Protection Agency National Estuary Program

Project_Description: This project is part of the overall management plan for the Florida Institute for Saltwater Heritage (F.I.S.H.) Preserve, including acquisition of several holdings, removal of exotics and habitat restoration on the entire site, and the creation of an interpretive trail system and museum. There was also the opportunity to improve a storm water pond adjacent to the property.
Habitat_Description: 100 acre preserve consisting of coastal wetlands (mangroves), uplands, tidal streams and freshwater ponds.

Project_Name: Siesta Key Tax Deed Lots Acquisition
Project_Description: Acquisition of coastal beach and dune property through the Sarasota County Environmental Land Acquisition Program  (ELAP) Program
Habitat_Description: Coastal beach and dune properties

Project_Description: Prescribed fire of pyrogenic habitats within the urban interface with Manatee County coastal preserves. Project benefits allows for the natural recruitment of habitats; including bird and other wildlife habitats.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland habitats

Project_Description: Riverview High School, a public high school in Sarasota County, completed an exotic vegetation removal project on their campus with help from an SBEP bay partners grant and other local matching funds. Students removed Brazilian pepper, mahoe trees and cogan grass from the shoreline and planted native vegetation to help stabilize the shoreline. Phillippi Creek now serves as a living laboratory for students, teachers and the public. Project benefits include educational opportunities, increase bird habitat, and erosion control.
Habitat_Description: Oligohaline shoreline along Sarasota's largest tidal tributary.

Project_Description: Sarasota Audubon society dug and planted a bioswale at their new wildlife viewing and nature center located at the Celery Field park.  Project benefits include water quality improvement and increase bird habitat.
Habitat_Description: Restored upland field and wetland system

Project_Description: This major restoration project consisted of the construction, enhancement or preservation of 120 acres of complex estuarine and coastal habitats. Restoration activities included clearing, grading and planting. Major habitat types resulting from this project include: fresh water ponds (1.22 acres); fresh water marshes (1.3 acres); saltmarsh island with tidal flats (5.21 acres); oyster bars (2.06 acres); live oak hammocks (25.54 acres); cedar hammocks (8.39 acres); coastal/tropical hammocks (8.64 acres) and pine flatwoods (14.44 acres). Also created were open salt water channels with tidal connections to the bay. Finally, viewing mounds, vegetative screens and other amenities for wildlife interactions were constructed as well.  The project will protect open space, present recreational activities, educational opportunities, as well as increase bird, other wildlife and fish habitats.
Habitat_Description: Mixture of coastal upland and wetland habitats
Partners: SWFWMD, Conservation Foundation of the Gulf Coast, SBEP

Project_Description: A series of artificial reef modules were deployed in Sarasota Bay to increase fish habitat.
Habitat_Description: Three permitted artificial reef sites in Manatee County were deployed in waters of Sarasota Bay.

Project_Description: Acquisition of property to provide a corridor between the Robinson and Perico Preserves in Manatee County.  Project will preserve and protect open space.
Habitat_Description: Mangrove and coastal upland habitats

Project_Name: Sarasota Bay Watershed Exotic Species Management
Project_Description: Exotic species management control via hand removal and selective herbicide application.  Project benefits include protecting/preserving open space for the natural recruitment of habitat, increase bird and other wildlife habitats.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland and wetland habitats

Project_Name: Sarasota Bay 34th Street Oyster Habitat Creation
Project_Description: Creation of one acre of oyster habitat in northern Sarasota Bay. Four twenty-foot diameter reefs were created using fossil shell. The perimeter was defined using shell bags while the interior of each reef contained loose shell. Coir fiber mesh bags were used instead of plastic to reduce marine pollution.
Habitat_Description: Habitat consists of four twenty-foot diameter intertidal oyster reefs placed on a shallow sand bar in northern Sarasota Bay. The complete reef structure encompasses one acre of bay bottom.

Project_Description: Along the scenic highway are two boat ramps, several water craft launches, Palma Sola Causeway Park, and Robinson Preserve, Perico, and Neal Preserves. Four locations along the highway were degraded from vehicles driving to the shoreline edge. This project removed exotic vegetation from four acres along the highway and planted one acre with native plants.
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland and shoreline habitats on the south bank of the Manatee River

Project_Name: Red Bug Slough Preserve exotic vegetation removal
Project_Description: Volunteers removed one acre of exotic vegetation within the park boundaries
Habitat_Description: Wooded upland county park and preerve

Project_Name: North Water Tower Park exotic vegetation removal
Project_Description: Volunteers removed one acre of invasive vegetation within the park boundaries
Habitat_Description: Urban wooded park within the City of Sarasota

Project_Description: Volunteers removed one acre of exotic vegetation within this Sarasota County park/preserve
Habitat_Description: Wooded upland City of Sarasota park/preserve.

Project_Description: Removal of mature invasive Australian pine trees from one acre of coastal upland habitat
Habitat_Description: Coastal upland on barrier island preserve

Project_Description: Removal of exotic vegetative species including hardwoods and invasive grasses.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetlands and adjacent uplands

Project_Description: This project had several elements: Removal of exotic vegetation, planting of native vegetation and the re-introduction of gopher tortoises through a Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission waif tortoise permit
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetlands and adjacent uplands
Main_Funding_Source: Coastal Partnership Initiative Grant; Manatee County

Project_Description: Removal of exotic vegetation species, including invasive hardwoods and grasses
Habitat_Description: Upland park and open space; freshwater wetlands

Habitat_Description: small coastal dune area on barrier island

Habitat_Description: Shoreline and intertidal oyster habitat

Habitat_Description: Coastal dunes adjacent to Sarasota Bay

Project_Description: Control and removal of exotic plant species including exotic hardwoods and invasive grasses.
Habitat_Description: Coastal uplands and intermittent wetalnds

Project_Description: The Neal Preserve Exotic Species Management project; a coastal wetland and upland habitat project in Manatee County. The Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FEPPC) categorize exotic/invasive plants according to levels of potential invasion and spreading.  The project consist of control of FLEPPC category 1 and 2 species, mostly exotic hardwoods and removal of invasive grasses through herbicide applications on ten acres.  Project benefits include protection and improvement of birds and other wildlife habitat.  This project also supports the Freshwater and Saltwater Wetlands Action 1.6. and Remove exotic noxious plants action of the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan (CCMP).
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Description: This project is to create 100 linear feet of Oyster Habitat at Robinson Preserve located in Manatee County.  A volunteer event to place oyster shell bags along an eroding shoreline within Robinson Preserve.  The project benefits include erosion control and the protection/improvement to/for increase habitat for fish/shellfish.  This project supports the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan (CCMP) Citizens Participation Chapter Action 5.1.; Encourage citizen engagement in environmental monitoring; Fisheries and Other Living Resources Chapter Action 4.2.; Establish oyster reefs in appropriate locations in Sarasota Bay.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine shoreline and shallow subtidal zone

Project_Name: Tom Bennett Park Exotic Species Management
Project_Description: This upland woods park and open space project consist of exotic species management control of 20 acres in the Tom Bennett Park in Manatee County.  The Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FEPPC) categorize exotic/invasive plants according to levels of potential invasion and spreading. Control of FLEPPC category 1 & 2 plant species, mostly exotic hardwoods and invasive grasses, through herbicide applications.  The project benefits include protection/improvement for increase/improved habitat for birds and other wildlife.  It also has associated educational and recreational opportunities. This project supports actions of the SBEP CCMP; Freshwater and Saltwater Wetlands Action 1.6. Remove exotic noxious plants.
Habitat_Description: Upland park of woods and open space

Project_Description: The 40 acre Perico Preserve Exotic Species Management project is located in Manatee County.  Habitat establishment period and adaptive management events at this site consisted of repeated herbicide treatments of weedy species to remove and control invasive vegetation and to provide for natural vegetation growth to increase bird and other wildlife habitats.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Description: The project involves 2.5 acres in Ungarelli Preserve located in Manatee County.  Exotic Species Management project Control of Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FLEPPC) Category 1 and 2 species consisting mostly of exotic hardwoods and invasive grasses primarily through herbicide applications to control/remove invasive vegetation to protect and provide increase habitats for birds and other wildlife.  The FEPPC categorize exotic/invasive plants according to levels of potential invasion and spreading.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Name: Robinson Preserve Expansion Exotic Species Management
Project_Description: One hundred twenty five acres in Robinson Preserve; a expansion exotic species management effort in Manatee County to control/remove invasive vegetation. This project primarily consisted of mowing expansion areas to support erosion control plantings and prevent establishment of specific weeds prior to planned revegetation effort. Project benefits include maintenance for protection/improvement to provide for increase bird and other wildlife habitat.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Description: This project is a prescribed burn of 15 acres at Robinson Preserve located in Manatee County.  The prescribed fire application consisted of normal prescribed fire for maintenance of pyrogenic habitats.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Name: Leffis Key Preserve Exotic Species Management
Project_Description: The Leffis Key Preserve Exotic Species Management of 2 acres in Manatee County.  This project involved the control of the Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FLEPPC) category 1 & 2 exotic plant species, mostly exotic hardwoods and invasive grasses, through herbicide applications. The FEPPC categorize exotic/invasive plants according to levels of potential invasion and spreading.  Project maintenance benefits include the protection/improvement to provide for increased habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats.

Project_Description: Acquisition of freshwater wetland and upland property. Habitat types include mesic flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods, baygall and blackwater streams. Native flora include longleaf pine, slash pine, saw palmetto, fox grape, elephant's foot, chalky bluestem, red maple, redbay and laurel oak. Exotics to be removed include west Indian marshgrass, caesarweed, wedelia and Brazilian pepper. Native wildlife include gopher tortoise, white-tailed deer and bobcat.
Habitat_Description: Mesic flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods, baygall, and blackwater stream
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota County Environmentally Sensitive Lands Protection Program

Project_Name: New College of Florida Native Plantings
Project_Description: New College Foundation conducted a planting effort of native vegetation on o.5 acres in a detention pond adjacent to their restored native shoreline to protect/improve/provide increased habitat for birds. This project supports the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan (CCMP) Action; Freshwater and Saltwater Wetlands Action 1.2.; Enhance, restore and create wetlands throughout the Sarasota Bay region.
Habitat_Description: Coastal saltwater wetlands

Project_Description: Robinson Preserve is exotic species maintenance effort of 50 acres of coastal wetland and upland habitats located in Manatee County.  The Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FEPPC) categorize exotic/invasive plants according to levels of potential invasion and spreading. Control of Florida Exotic Plant Pest Council (FLEPPC) category 1 & 2 species, mostly exotic hardwoods and invasive grasses, through herbicide applications.  Benefits of the project include protection/improvement for increased bird and wildlife habitats.  This project supports the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan Action; Freshwater and Saltwater Wetlands Action 1.6. Remove exotic noxious plants.
Habitat_Description: Coastal wetland and upland habitats

Project_Description: This is the Orchid Oaks environmental shoreline enhancement project. The Orchid Oaks Condominium Association removed exotic vegetation and planted native vegetation along four acres in a creekside preserve.  Project benefits include  protection/improvement to provide increased habitat for birds and other wildlife. This project supports the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (SBEP) Comprehensive Conservation Management Plan (CCMP) Action; Freshwater and Saltwater Wetlands Action 1.2.; Enhance, restore and create wetlands throughout the Sarasota Bay region.
Habitat_Description: Freshwater creek shoreline

Project_Description: This land acquisition of 1.15 acres of undeveloped coastal property is located in the Little Sarasota Bay segment of Sarasota Bay. The property consists of a mangrove fringed shoreline with native sea grape, southern red cedar, oak and slash pine. Exotic vegetation removed include phoenix reclinata, Norfolk pine and Brazilian pepper. Benefits of this land acquisition is to provide protection for other wildlife habitats; improve water quality and to allow for climate change adaptation/impacts.
Habitat_Description: Undeveloped coastal habitat

Project_Description: This project consisted of .01 acres of dune creation along a section of Coquina Beach in Manatee County. The beach nourishment project provided high visibility for outreach/education opportunities while preventing sand migration into handicap access walkways.
Habitat_Description: Coastal dunes in Manatee County

Project_Name: South Gate Community Association creekside habitat enhancement
Project_Description: The South Gate Community Association habitat enhancement project.  The South Gate community Association was the lead implementer on the project in partnership with Sarasota Bay Estuary Program.  The project consisted of removal of exotic vegetation and planted native vegetation on their privately owned creek side property.    Benefits of the project provide protection and improvement to increase habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Freshwater Phillippi Creek shoreline enhancement

Project_Description: The Sherwood Forest homeowner association (lead) SBEP partnered; planted native vegetation around their stormwater pond.  Project benefits include enhancement, protection and improve/increase habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Homeowner Association stormwater ponds

Project_Name: Pine Island Preserve Invasive Plant Maintenance
Project_Description: This project addresses annual maintenance of exotic and invasive vegetation; specifically 14 acres on Pine Island Preserve in the Braden River, located in Manatee county. County staff and volunteers employed a variety of techniques to control a broad spectrum of invasive plant species to improve/provide habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Mesic flatwoods dominated island with mangrove swamp and Juncus marsh fringes
Main_Funding_Source: Manatee County Parks and Natural Resources Ad Valorem and Water Utilities

Project_Name: Robinson Expansion Land Bridge Native Planting Project
Project_Description: Staff from the Manatee County Natural Resources division planted 300 native cabbage palms along the land bridges within the Robinson Preserve expansion property. These palms serve as natural buffers and provide shade for preserve visitors and provide protection and habitat for other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Coastal preserve consisting of uplands, woods and saltwater wetlands.

Project_Description: This first-of-its kind volunteer oyster restoration project took place in July, 2019. Over forty volunteers and 15 staff from Manatee County and Sarasota Bay Estuary Program bagged, transported and placed over 6 tons of recycled oyster shell at Perico Preserve. The recycled shell came from a new program from the non profit organization START (Solutions to Avoid Red Tide), who obtained the shell from local seafood restaurants. This material was placed in the intertidal zone as cultch material to attract oyster spat and stabilize the shoreline.
Habitat_Description: Intertidal shoreline along newly created tidal wetland within Perico Preserve

Project_Description: Sarasota County purchased this property on December 28, 2018 through it's Neighborhood Parkland Program. It lies within the Little Sarasota Bay watershed. The shoreline is mangrove fringed with a deteriorating seawall. Sarasota County is planning improvements to the property including the removal of nuisance vegetation and creating a living shoreline.
Habitat_Description: This 2.79 acre bay front parcel has 225 linear feet of shoreline in Sarasota County. The parcel is primarily open space with native and exotic vegetation.

Project_Description: This project involves the annual maintenance of exotic and invasive vegetation on Manatee County's five coastal preserves (Emerson, Robinson, Perico, Ungarelli, and Neal Preserves. County staff and volunteers employ a variety of techniques to control a broad spectrum of invasive plant species on these valuable nature preserves.
Habitat_Description: Habitats contain a mixture of created restored and extant estuarine and coastal uplands, including coastal hammock, mangrove swamp, coastal grasslands with minor Mesic flatwoods and scrub components.
Main_Funding_Source: Manatee County PNR-Ad Valorem and Water Utilities

Project_Description: Manatee County Natural Resources staff installed 400 native buttonwood trees along a corridor between the Robinson and Perico Preserves. These trees, when fully mature, will serve as a buffer between these preserves and the surrounding developments.
Habitat_Description: Coastal uplands and wetlands connection two natural preserves.

Project_Name: Johnson Preserve on the Braden River
Project_Description: Manatee County acquired 43.82 acres of forest/woodland for inclusion in its protected county natural lands program.
Habitat_Description: Flatwoods and forested freshwater wetlands
Main_Funding_Source: Manatee County and Community Foundation of the Gulf Coast
Lead_Implementer: Manatee County Parks & Natural Resources Department

Project_Description: Manatee County and the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program partnered to create 2 acres of new oyster habitat in Perico Bayou. SBEP assisted with project design, permit acquisition and project implementation. To celebrate National Estuaries Week in September, SBEP staff & volunteers teamed up with the Tampa Bay Estuary Program in recruiting over 100 volunteers to help build the reefs.  Project benefits include; improve water quality and provide for fish and shellfish habitat.
Habitat_Description: Shallow estuarine waters over sandy substrate which is ideal for creating new oyster habitat

Project_Name: Boulevard of the Arts Living Shoreline Restoration Project
Project_Description: Through this program, the Florida Department of Environmental Protection awarded the City of Sarasota $187,972 to use nature-based infrastructure to enhance and strengthen the shoreline along Sarasota Bay. Project funds were used to increase shoreline resiliency along Sarasota Bay by removing a degraded seawall and replacing it with a softer, sloped rip-rap design and to restore a living shoreline and breakwater. This is the first phase of a years-long city initiative to transform a 53-acre site into a more inclusive and welcoming community waterfront destination.  Project provides protection from erosion and adaption to climate impacts.
Habitat_Description: Estuarine shoreline habitat
Main_Funding_Source: Florida Department of Environmental Protection Florida Resilient Coastlines Program

Project_Name: Orchard Oaks Preserve Restoration Project at Phillippi Creek
Project_Description: This project involved exotic/nuisance plant removal and native plant installation within 1 acre located along the 2,000 feet of the Phillippi Creek shoreline. A contractor performed the more labor-intensive work of exotic control and most of the native plantings. Trees were cut, stems mulched, and stumps treated with herbicide. Roots were left maintain soil stabilization. Exotic vines, grasses, and groundcover were treated with a foliar application. Twenty native plant species were installed to stabilize the soils and help recolonize the areas with desirable plants. Remaining plants were installed during the volunteer event on April 13, 2019 as well as hand removal of Brazilian pepper, carrotwood, and caesarweed.
Habitat_Description: Wooded shoreline along Phillippi Creek, the largest tidal tributary to Sarasota Bay
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (EPA Section 320 funds)

Project_Description: This project is the Red Bug Slough planting project; located in Sarasota, County. This site was formerly a 6.2 acre monoculture of Brazilian pepper trees. This project was intended to restore it to a riparian hardwood forest. Twenty-seven volunteers planted 654 native plants over two separate event days. Fifty native trees and 604 native shrubs, wildflowers, grasses and ferns were planted to protect and provide habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: This site was formerly a 6.2 acre monoculture of Brazilian pepper trees. This project is intended to restore it to a riparian hardwood forest.

Project_Description: This project involved the installation of 400 native buttonwood trees on the recently purchased natural lands that separated Robinson Preserve from Perico Preserve. These trees, when fully mature, will form a natural buffer between the Preserves and surrounding development.  The project help to provide and protect habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Restored and natural coastal upland preserves

Project_Description: The project goal was to increase the vegetative diversity of Bowlees Creek Sanctuary Island.This was achieved by adding 24 species of plants. In total, 176 native coastal berm trees, shrubs and forbs were planted along a cleared path meandering through the center of the island to protect and provide habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Bowlees Creek is an estuarine island in Sarasota Bay that was restored in 2010. Since then, several trash cleanups and exotic vegetation maintenance events have kept the island in its restored condition.
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program (EPA Section 320 funds)

Project_Description: This project consisted of the acquisition of this mesic, wooded parcel adjacent to Phillippi Creek, the largest tributary to Sarasota Bay within its watershed.
Habitat_Description: This parcel consists of upland mesic hammock
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota County Environmentally Sensitive Lands Protection Program (ESLPP), Neighborhood Parkland Acquisition Program ad valorem tax
Lead_Implementer: Sarasota County Parks and Natural Resources

Project_Name: Blackburn Point Living Shoreline Erosion Control Project
Project_Description: Heavy erosion was occurring along the estuarine shoreline of the Park. Erosion mitigation and shoreline enhancements took place in two phases. The first phase consisted of installing coir logs to stabilize the shoreline. The second phase included the planting of aquatic and terrestrial plants, including red mangroves, green buttonwood, railroad vine sea oxeye daisy and salt meadow cordgrass. Mature Australian pines were removed from the shoreline to protect public safety and create the space for native vegetation.
Habitat_Description: Eroding estuarine shoreline

Project_Name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge Exotic Plant Control - Cogon grass 2013
Project_Description: Non-native invasive cogon grass was treated and killed in upland habitats and right-of-ways of the refuge.
Habitat_Description: Coastal marsh, pine flatwoods, and scrub located within the Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge. The refuge is bounded by the Indian River Lagoon and Atlantic ocean.

Project_Name: FISH Preserve Coastal Wetlands Restoration and Enhancement Phase III
Project_Description: This project phase consisted of controlling exotic invasive plants, excavating a tidal creek and marsh, and planting beneficial native grasses to enhance hydrology and wildlife habitats.
Habitat_Description: Coastal hammock habitats consisting of tidal creeks, mangroves and saltmarsh
Main_Funding_Source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission; Sarasota Bay Estuary Program

Project_Name: Hudson Bayou In-Stream Restoration and Water Quality Improvements
Project_Description: This seven year project aimed to enhance the drainage and storage, reduce pollutant and sediment loading, preserve tree islands, and improve native habitat of a tributary to Sarasota Bay (Hudson Bayou). This project consisted of eight elements: 1. Parking Drainage & Bioswale. 2. Exotic Vegetation Removal. 3. Skimmer.  4. Slope Restoration & Upland Planting.  5. Vegetative Filter Marsh. 6. Tree Island Preservation. 7. Sediment Sump and Dredge Silt Removal. 8. Natural Buffer Area. The enhancements help treat upstream runoff from 973 acres, or about 40% of the Hudson Bayou watershed. All together, the water quality treatments are estimated to remove about 25% of total nitrogen and 67% of total suspended solids annually.
Habitat_Description: Urban tributary to Sarasota Bay
Main_Funding_Source: Southwest Florida Water Management District Cooperative Funding Initiative; Sarasota County

Project_Description: Volunteers from the SBEP Bay Guardians program were recruited to assist with the deployment of material to create a 0.5 acre oyster bar. Cultch material was donated from a local shell recycling program.
Habitat_Description: Intertidal sand bottom with native oysters nearby

Project_Name: Chrysopsis floridana Planting at Perico Preserve
Project_Description: This project consisted of growing out and planting 0.2 acres of previously restored habitat at Perico Preserve with the Federally endangered plant species, Harissa aborginum.
Habitat_Description: Coastal plain and wetlands
Main_Funding_Source: Manatee County Parks and Natural Resources Department
Lead_Implementer: Manatee County Parks and Natural Resources Department

Project_Name: Camp Honi Honta Pollinator Garden Project
Project_Description: This project consisted of converting a former sod maintenance area to an important pollinator garden through the removal of the sodded areas and planting native vegetation
Habitat_Description: This property was a former sod maintained parcel.

Project_Description: This oasis of nature in urban Manatee County is home to an amazing diversity of plants and animals not normally seen in similar suburban areas. It is a piece of ‘Old Florida” with mature live oaks, tall longleaf pines, important wetlands that store water preventing flooding, and imperiled swallowtail kites and gopher tortoises. The land’s riverfront and floodplain forests are part of a corridor linking natural habitat along the Braden River, which serves as a drinking water source for the City of Bradenton.  This project consisted of the application of beneficial fire, prescribed burn, to maintain the viability of this important upland preserve.
Habitat_Description: Habitat consists of upland forests and woodlands.

Project_Name: Coquina Beach Storm Damage Restoration Project
Project_Description: Coquina Beach Storm Damage Restoration Project located in Coastal sandy beach in Manatee County, FL.  This project consisted of the placement of 80,00 cubic yards of sand at Coquina Beach, Manatee County, to offset the loss of sand due to storm erosion.
Habitat_Description: Coastal sandy beach in Manatee County, FL

Project_Description: Perico Bayou oyster reef creation. Shallow sub-tidal and inter-tidal unvegetated bay bottom that served as the substrate to construct new oyster reefs. Manatee County staff created a 0.2 acre oyster in Perico Bayou using recycled oyster from local restaurants. Shell was provided through the Gulf Coast Oyster Recycling Program (GCORR).
Habitat_Description: Shallow sub-tidal and inter-tidal unvegetated bay bottom that served as the substrate to construct new oyster reefs.

Project_Description: Bridge Street Artificial Reef Creation.  Sand/shell bottom in nearshore Gulf of Mexico.  This artificial reef project was constructed in 35 feet of water and is located 2.5 nautical miles west of Passage Key Inlet. The reef was built using ~400 tons of 4-16 foot long reinforced concrete culvert. A cement reef module standing 8 feet tall by 10 feet wide and weighing 5200 pounds was also deployed.  This new reef habitat will augment two previous deployments which consisted of a 120 ft x 45 ft steel barge and ~200 tons of concrete culvert. These complex artificial reef habitats create recreational fishing and diving areas which provide a substantial economic benefit to Manatee County.
Habitat_Description: Sand/shell bottom in nearshore Gulf of Mexico
Lead_Implementer: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

Project_Description: Multi-phase living shoreline enhancement project aimed to protect the shoreline from erosion, along with adding quality habitat for aquatic and upland wildlife. Phase 1: Added coir logs to protect shoreline from erosion, along with planting 50+ red mangroves to add to erosion protection and provide habitat for wildlife. Phase 2: extend living shoreline by removing invasive vegetation and add additional coir logs. Plant additional red mangroves, along with upland plants. Phase 3 (in progress): added roughly 500 linear feet of oyster bags.
Habitat_Description: Coastal mangrove fringe located at Blackburn Point Park

Project_Name: Johnson Preserve Invasive Plant Control Project
Project_Description: This oasis of nature in urban Manatee County is home to an amazing diversity of plants and animals not normally seen in similar suburban areas. It is a piece of ‘Old Florida” with mature live oaks, tall longleaf pines, important wetlands that store water preventing flooding, and imperiled swallowtail kites and gopher tortoises. The land’s riverfront and floodplain forests are part of a corridor linking natural habitat along the Braden River, which serves as a drinking water source for the City of Bradenton.  This project activity consisted of targeted treatment of exotic cogon grass and other invasive exotic plants to maintain the native integrity of this valuable urban preserve.
Habitat_Description: Project habitat contains natural forests and woodlands.

Project_Name: FISH Preserve Phase 4 Exotic Tree Removal
Project_Description: To preserve the natural habitat which the commercial fishing industry depends, the community of Cortez, Florida raised funds to purchase this property in 2010. Encompassing over 100 acres of environmentally sensitive land east of Cortez, for hundreds of years this site has survived as an important fisheries habitat for Sarasota Bay south of Cortez referred to as "the kitchen."  The restoration of this property, called the FISH Preserve. A dense stand of mature Australian Pines were removed in preparation for the final restoration activities.
Habitat_Description: Altered coastal forested uplands

Project_Description: This project consisted of the creation of artificial patch reef habitat within the shallow of the Gulf of Mexico along Bradenton Beach, FL and habitat includes Shallow, coastal artificial reef complex in Manatee County waters. Project benefit to provide habitat for other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Shallow, coastal artificial reef complex in Manatee County waters

Project_Name: Robinson Preserve Expansion: FY22 Habitat Restoration Activities
Project_Description: A variety of restoration activities were conducted at Robinson Preserve Expansion during FY22. Manatee County Parks and Natural Resources staff coordinated staffing and volunteer events to complete the work. Restoration events included: HEPAM exotic vegetation removal, native tree planting, native grass and shrub plantings and deployment of vertical oyster gardens.
Habitat_Description: Coastal forest, woodlands and wetlands

Project_Name: Perico Bayou Oyster Bar Creation Area Supplementation
Project_Description: Shallow water habitat with substrate consisting of mollusk shells.  Addition of supplemental oyster cultch on an existing permitted oyster bar originally created in 2021 to provide habitat for fish/shellfish.
Habitat_Description: Shallow water habitat with substrate consisting of mollusk shells

Project_Description: Manatee County Parks and Recreation regularly employs prescribed fire application to its managed coastal resources to maintain healthy and vibrant native habitats. Matrix of coastal upland and estuarine wetland habitats, including mangrove forests, saltmarsh and saltern. This project involved preparation for and application of beneficial fire at their coastal preserves during FY22.
Habitat_Description: Matrix of coastal upland and estuarine wetland habitats, including mangrove forests, saltmarsh and saltern

Project_Description: The restoration of Rattlesnake Island and Turner Key consisted of several elements. The first element focused on the removal and/or treatment of invasive Australian pine trees (APs). Select APs were cut down and trunks were places along the edge of the nature trail. Branches were chipped and placed along the trail. Other APs were killed in place to create future habitat for nesting birds, particularly ospreys. A sign was installed describing the project and its benefits to wildlife and recreational opportunities. Finally, nearly 2,000 native plants, consisting of six tree and 5 shrub/ground cover species, were planted by volunteers and Sarasota County staff.
Habitat_Description: These estuarine spoil islands were created during the construction of the Intracoastal Waterway in the 1960s. These types of spoil islands throughout Sarasota Bay generally consist of dense forests of upland exotic tree species, including Australian pines, carrotwood trees and Brazilian pepper. Rattlesnake Island and Turner Key were dominated by Australian Pines.
Main_Funding_Source:
The Community Foundation for Northeast Florida
West Coast Inland Navigation District

Project_Name: Blackburn Point Shoreline Habitat and Stabilization Project
Project_Description: This project was designed to stabilize the shoreline and create intertidal habitat through the following methods: removal of invasive Australian pine trees, deployment of coir logs, oyster bags and native vegetation planting. Benefits include erosion control and habitat for fish/shellfish.
Habitat_Description: The estuarine shoreline at Blackburn Point Park, a Sarasota County Park in Sarasota Bay, has undergone severe erosion over the past several years.
Main_Funding_Source:
The Community Foundation for Northeast Florida
Sarasota County Restoration Fund
Sarasota Bay Estuary Program
Lead_Implementer: Sarasota County Parks and Natural Resources

Project_Description: Leffis Key was created in the early 2000's through cooperation between the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program and Manatee County. Over the years, the native habitats have been altered by subtle changes in sea level and other causes. This project consisted of replanting the various zones with hydrologically placed native plants. The project, again led by the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program and Manatee County Natural Resources, solicited volunteers to plant native groundcover to promote diversity and habitat enhancement.
Habitat_Description:
Leffis Key is a created estuarine island in upper Sarasota Bay. It consists of a matrix of estuarine wetland habitats, 
 mangrove wetlands, saltmarsh and salterns.

Project_Description: Project includes pilot level seagrass plantings and the operation of two seagrass nurseries. Seagrass plantings utilize Halodule wrightii and herbivory exclusion in an array. Also includes the operation of two seagrass nurseries, located in Rockledge and Melbourne Beach. Halodule wrightii will grow for out planting and other species will raised in test tanks for experimentation.
Habitat_Description: Site selection, planting, monitoring, and maintenance of 6 seagrass restoration sites at 6 locations located throughout Brevard County. Plantings have been conducted in all three basins in shallow areas with historic seagrass coverage.
Main_Funding_Source: Indian River Lagoon National Estuary Program

Project_Description: This was a volunteer event to plant native vegetation at Robinson Expansion on 4 acres in Manatee County to promote diversity and habitat enhancement to protect and provide habitat for birds and other wildlife.
Habitat_Description: Robinson Expansion consists of a variety of coastal and wetland habitats.

Project_Name: Crooked Creek Condominium Association Habitat Restoration
Project_Description: Water flowing through the Crooked Creek Condominium Complex originates from Red Bug Slough and eventually drains back into the slough. Removing invasive plants and replanting native species along these shoreline areas benefit water quality in Red Bug Slough, Phillippi Creek, and ultimately Sarasota Bay. Crooked Creek’s volunteer residents planted native species along the creek, .5 acres, to prevent further shoreline erosion, help filter the water that flows through our development, and enhance the wildlife habitat.
Habitat_Description: Private property adjacent to Red Bug slough, which drains to Phillipi Creek, the largest tributary to Sarasota Bay.
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program Bay Partners Grant

Project_Description: Orchard Oaks abuts Phillipi Creek, the largest tributary to Sarasota Bay. The Orchard Oaks Condominium Association has received multi-year Bay Partners grants to restore the natural habitats within this hardwood hammock and shoreline. In FY 23, they oversaw the removal of exotic trees, shrubs, vines, and groundcover from the community property, on three acres, planted native vegetation and installed two bioswales directly downstream of untreated onsite stormwater conveyances adjacent to Phillipi Creek.
Habitat_Description: Orchard Oaks property consists of Hardwood hammocks and littoral zones along Phillipi Creek, Sarasota.
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program Bay Partners Grant

Project_Description: This project consisted of association members overseeing pond restoration efforts through the planting of nearly 3,500 feet of shoreline with native littoral vegetation.  Project benefits include erosion control, climate adaptation & resiliency and water quality improvements.
Habitat_Description: Stormwater ponds within the Vizcaya condominium association property.
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program Bay Partners Grant

Project_Name: Manatee County Coastal Preserves Prescribed Fire Applications
Project_Description: This project consists of the preparation for and application of beneficial fire on 77 acres to maintain the functional value of a variety of coastal upland and wetland habitats.
Habitat_Description: Habitat consists of a matrix of coastal upland and estuarine wetland habitats- mangrove swamp, saltmarsh, salt tern
Lead_Implementer: Manatee County Department of Natural Resources

Project_Description: This project consisted of cutting and mulching two dozen mature Australian pines on one acre from the restored coastal hammock located in the City of Sarasota.
Habitat_Description: Coastal hammock adjacent to North Lido Beach
Main_Funding_Source: Private donation to the Environmental Fund of the Gulf Coast Community Foundation

Project_Description: Volunteers gathered on Saturday, August 19 to plant 8,200 square feet of open meadow with nearly 4,000 native grasses and wildflowers.  All 2" liners on about 1.5' centers.  Several small areas were excluded because another non-selective herbicide treatment was planned before planting those areas.
Habitat_Description: Perico Preserve is a coastal wetland and open upland meadow in western Manatee County. This dormant agricultural land was originally restored in 2016.

Project_Description: Oyster habitat restoration in Sarasota Bay requires a steady supply of recycled oyster shell. This project arranged with eight local Manatee County seafood restaurants to save discarded oyster shell. From January through May 2023, Waste Pro picked up this shell and deposited it at the Nest Educational Center at Robinson Preserve for use in habitat restoration projects. These projects included intertidal oyster reefs and vertical oyster gardens (VOGs).
Habitat_Description: Intertidal oyster reefs and vertical oyster gardens throughout the Sarasota Bay estuary.
Lead_Implementer: Manatee County Department of Natural Resources

Project_Description:
The Manatee Fish and Game Association enhanced the vegetation composition of 2.3 acres of upland and wetland habitats on the Bowlees Creek Bird Sanctuary Island located in Sarasota Bay just south of the mouth of Bowlees Creek.
Vegetation Enhancement was conducted by Altec Lakes and Natural Areas (a contractor) as specified and overseen by Damon Moore with MFG. The initial treatment and biomass reduction event occurred in October of 2022 and was successful at reducing weedy growth and treating invasive exotic species that have become established on the island.
Habitat_Description: Bowlees Creek Bird Sanctuary Island is a restored spoil island in Sarasota Bay.
Main_Funding_Source: Sarasota Bay Estuary Program Bay Partners Grant
Lead_Implementer: The Manatee Fish and Game Association

Project_Description: On September 1, 2022, as part of our shoreline stabilization project at Blackburn Point Park's center node, we strategically installed oyster bags along the shoreline. Unfortunately, later that month, Hurricane Ian passed through and had a significant impact on some of the bags we had initially placed. In response to the damage caused by the hurricane, on June 12, 2023, we took proactive measures and added 210 more oyster bags in the affected area to reinforce and fortify the shoreline. Additionally, during this time, we also replaced coir logs where necessary to directly stabilize the shore, ensuring a resilient and enduring solution.
Habitat_Description: Blackburn Point Park consists of several shoreline habitats including a mangrove fringe and oyster reefs.

Project_Description: As part of a mangrove project, our team planted 60 new mangroves, contributing to the preservation and enhancement of this vital coastal ecosystem. To ensure continued access to the water and maintain a harmonious balance, existing mangroves underwent careful trimming or removal, allowing for proper management without compromising their overall health and ecological value. The mangrove project reflects our commitment to sustainable land management practices, where thoughtful conservation efforts are integrated with practical considerations. By planting new mangroves and managing existing ones, we are safeguarding the ecological integrity of the area while promoting public access and enjoyment of these valuable coastal resources.
Habitat_Description: North Lido Preserve contains a variety of upland and wetland habitats including coastal scrub and mangroves.

Project_Description: Oyster shells acquired from Manatee County were used to craft twenty VOGs (Vertical Oyster Gardens) and suspended them from a dock at Blackburn Point Park's Center Node. These VOGs are part of an effort aimed at enhancing the local marine environment and educating the public on the environmental benefits of oysters. VOGs are being monitor quarterly to measure their effectiveness in fostering oyster habitat and marine life in the area.
Habitat_Description: Blackburn Point Park consists of shoreline restoration habitats including a mangrove fringe and oyster shell shoreline stabilization.

Project_Name: Siesta Public Beach Native Species Planting
Project_Description:
County staff recently undertook a significant rerouting project. Three beach access points were carefully redesigned to ensure the integrity of the pedestrian trail while adhering to responsible land management practices.
We blocked off the old paths encroaching on sensitive areas. A diverse array of coastal species, including sea grape, sea oats, green buttonwood, railroad vine, and dune sunflower, were selected and planted. Project_Description: The goal of Tampa Bay Watch’s Community Oyster Reef Enhancement (CORE) program is to increase oyster populations in Tampa Bay while providing habitats for small organisms, preventing erosion, improving water quality, and promoting fish and wildlife habitats. The 2D Island Phase 2 Oyster Reef Creation Project consisted of the installation of oyster shell bags placed in the intertidal zone beneath the canopy of the mangroves. Each oyster shell bag was filled with fossilized shells and laid perpendicular to the shoreline in various arrangements based on substrate stability and shoreline slope. The shell bags were transported (by boat), unloaded, and placed at 2D Island by Tampa Bay Watch staff and volunteers .
Habitat_Description: 2D Island is a large spoil island located in Hillsborough Bay east of the mouth of the Alafia River. 2D Island was created in the late 1970’s as part of the Harbor Deepening Project. It is situated on the east side of the main channel into Port Tampa Bay and the north side of the channel into the Riverview Mosaic berth. Much of the eastern shoreline consists of mangrove habitat which has been eroding due to wave energy from increased ship and boat wake in the area, as well as from storm events.

Project_Name: Abercrombie Park Oyster Bar Creation Project
Project_Description: The goal of Tampa Bay Watch’s Community Oyster Reef Enhancement program is to increase oyster populations in Tampa Bay, while providing habitats for small organisms, preventing erosion, improving water quality and promoting fish and wildlife habitats. The Abercrombie Park Living Shoreline Creation Project consists of the installation of two types of substrate that provide a hard surface for oyster larvae to settle upon and grow, eventually forming a functioning reef: oyster reef balls (ORB) and oyster shell bags filled with fossilized and recycled oyster shell. Project_Name: Restoration of dragline ditched coastal wetlands in Volusia County, Florida: Phase 2
Project_Description: Dragline ditches are extensive networks of deep, wide ditches and spoil piles cut through historical coastal wetland habitat, severely reducing the acreage of wetlands remaining. The purpose of the ditches was to interrupt the life cycle of saltmarsh mosquitoes by altering their breeding sites. A systematic process for restoring coastal wetlands that have been dragline ditched has been developed. Dragline ditch restoration projects such as this one require the use of an amphibious excavator. An excavator was mounted on tracked pontoons, enabling them to access submerged areas. This low-bearing weight machine (less than 2 pounds per square inch) is owned and operated by Volusia County Mosquito Control. Vegetation was cleared from the spoil area and placed in the adjacent ditch. This process avoided burning the plants and permanently sequesters the carbon they contain. Spoil material was first moved to the side of the ditch. If additional material remained, the main ditch was narrowed. The area of the spoil pile and the newly filled ditch were carefully graded to the adjacent remaining wetland elevation. The result is that substantially more area is at coastal wetland elevation
Habitat_Description: Dragline ditch-impacted coastal wetands adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon.

Project_Name: Community Outreach and Restoration of Intertidal Oyster Reefs in Mosquito Lagoon
Project_Description: The restoration efforts occured in the Mosquito Lagoon within the waters of the Canaveral National Seashore. The restoration efforts required leveling dead margins and providing stabilized recruitment substrate for oysters (oyster restoration mats) over the leveled shell material. The mats prevent movement of the leveled material and provide an increase in the available oyster habitat and thus the number of live oysters, oyster clusters and associated oyster reef organisms. Leveling the dead margins was conducted either by an amphibious excavator operated by the Volusia County Mosquito Control, and hand raking by volunteers, if the excavator was not available.
Habitat_Description: Dead oyster reefs located in the Mosquito Lagoon section of the Indian River Lagoon. Shellfish ecosystems are likely among the most imperiled of all marine ecosystems, surpassing coral reefs, mangroves and seagrasses in the magnitude and geographic extent of loss. Oysters and oyster reef habitat have declined dramatically along the east coast of the United States over the past century due to habitat degradation, overharvesting, reduced water quality, and disease. In Florida, additional anthropogenic impacts have been documented in shallow-water locations with intense recreational boating activity. Wakes produced by recreational vessels cause extensive shell movement and sediment resuspension. This results in large piles of disarticulated shells along the seaward edges of reefs that extend up to one meter above the mean high water line. Reefs with these dead shell margins have significantly lower numbers of live oysters, 3-D oyster clusters, and faunal biodiversity. Dead margins also act as small islands and allow for retention and germination of both native (mangrove) and invasive (Brazilian pepper) flora, promoting changes from aquatic to terrestrial habitats.

Project_Description: Bowlees Creek Island is a 3.0-acre island located at the mouth of Bowlees Creek in Manatee County, Florida. This spoil island was created in the 1960’s by dredging within the adjacent coastal habitat. Bowlees Creek Island is managed by the Audubon of Florida’s Coastal Islands Program. The island is vegetated by wetland and upland species. The wetland areas are dominated by mangroves and fringed by buttonwood. The upland areas are dominated by the following exotic tres: Australian pine (Casuarina equisetifolia), Brazilian pepper (Schinus terebinthifolius) and carrotwood (Cupaniopsis anacardiodes). Due to the presence of healthy native vegetation covering approximately 50% of the island, the most effect strategy was the selective removal of the exotic species. A restoration plan was developed which identified areas of exotic trees to be eradicated. Many of the Australian pine had been previously treated with herbicide and were dead. However, the carrotwood and Brazilian pepper were still thriving on the island and were targeted for this project. Exotic removal was accomplished through mechanical and manual techniques. Because the project took place on an island, the cut trees were piled and burned. A few of the larger carrotwoods were left for ospreys (Pandion haliaetus) and other birds to utilize for nesting. Project_Description: This constitutes the second phase of restoration on this 100 acre site.
